title: ACRCP6-Integrated Rust Initiative: Program 3. Integrated Disease Management and Extension
description:
Cereal rust diseases continue to pose a significant and evolving threat to Australian wheat, barley and oat production. Wheat rust alone costs the Australian grains industry $147 million pa when controlled with genetics and current management practices, but predicted losses are close to $1.7 billion pa if no control occurs (Murray and Brennan, 2009). Rust pathogens are highly adaptable and have repeatedly overcome deployed genetic resistance and chemical control options, resulting in yield losses, increased fungicide use and rising production costs for growers. While the Australian Cereal Rust Control Program (ACRCP) has delivered strong outcomes over multiple phases, the increasing complexity of pathogen evolution (E.g. Yr15 virulent pathogen and BGYR pathogen evolution), fungicide sensitivity, loss of access to chemistry risk and climate driven disease pressure requires a more integrated and future focused investment approach.
The next phase will bring these activities together in a coordinated national initiative. It will strengthen rust surveillance, accelerate the development and use of durable genetic resistance, and improve integrated disease management across production systems. Expanding the program beyond wheat to include barley and oats will allow proven approaches and lessons to benefit the broader grains industry.
The Australian Cereal Rust Control Program Phase 6 (ACRCP6) – Integrated Rust Initiative will build on existing capability while addressing gaps in coordination, efficiency and preparedness for emerging rust threats. By supporting more durable crop resistance, responsible fungicide use and better-informed decisions by breeders, advisers and growers, the initiative aims to reduce the long-term cost and impact of cereal rust.
This procurement is specifically for the Integrated Disease Management (IDM) and Extension component of ACRCP6. GRDC is seeking a provider to identify priority rust management gaps, develop and update practical IDM strategies, and translate surveillance, crop resistance, seasonal risk and fungicide stewardship information into timely resources and advice for growers and advisers. The work will support more effective rust management, reduce reliance on reactive fungicide use and improve the grains industry’s long-term resilience.

Net blotches pose an escalating and urgent threat to Australian barley, costing the industry an estimated $122 million each year through disease-related yield losses, downgraded grain quality, and higher fungicide management costs. title: Understanding barriers and enablers to IPM adoption in Australian grains
description:
Australian grain growers are managing pests in an increasingly complex and constrained environment. Key challenges include increasing insecticide resistance, changing access to crop protection products, regulatory and market pressures, emerging and episodic pest threats, and the need to protect beneficial insects and biological control services while preserving the effectiveness of available chemistry.
GRDC has previously invested in integrated pest management (IPM) adoption, extension and research into the factors that influence practice change across a range of grain-growing regions and pest systems. This provides an important foundation, but much of the earlier adoption work was undertaken before the current level of pressure from insecticide resistance and chemical access constraints, and before more recent changes in how growers and advisers access information and make pest-management decisions.
GRDC is seeking a suitably qualified provider or multidisciplinary team to undertake an independent opportunity analysis examining the barriers, enablers and pathways influencing practical IPM adoption in Australian grain systems. The analysis will draw on existing evidence, current and previous GRDC and industry investments, available tools and resources, relevant experience from other agricultural industries and international cropping systems, and the perspectives of growers, advisers, researchers, extension and adoption practitioners, and other relevant stakeholders.
The work must consider the technical, behavioural, advisory, commercial and broader system-level factors influencing grower and adviser practice change. It must establish a contemporary understanding of current IPM adoption capability, barriers and enabling conditions; assess what has changed since previous IPM adoption and extension investments; and identify the audiences, circumstances and delivery approaches where future effort is most likely to improve practical adoption outcomes.
GRDC requires practical, evidence-based and decision-ready recommendations to guide the design of future research, development, extension and adoption investments in IPM. The work is intended to focus on adoption and practice-change pathways rather than undertake a detailed technical review of individual pests or pest-management tactics. Where technical limitations are affecting adoption, these should be identified as matters that may require further research and development.

description:

This call builds on the approach of the Grain Automate Program.

title: Operational Energy Transitions Defence Research Centre Lead Partner
description:
The Commonwealth is undertaking two separate but related approaches to market (ATM) in parallel to support the establishment of the OET DRC and the delivery of its Inaugural Research Projects (IRPs). The processes being undertaken include:
a. ATM ID 13016 Lead Partner Request For Tender (RFT) (this RFT): to engage a supplier as a Lead Partner to provide research leadership and expertise at the program and project level for the OET DRC; and
b. ATM ID 13457 Contributing Partner Request For Information (RFI) (separate process): to engage with the market for the purposes of:
(i) understanding market capability and potential suppliers that align with, and have interest in, research related to the OET DRC; and
(ii) informing the development and conduct of this Lead Partner RFT as well as future procurement processes.
The Contributing Partner RFI:
a. is separate from, does not form part of, this RFT; and
b. is governed by its own separate process. Further details on the Contributing Partner ATM can be found on AusTender.
You are invited to submit a tender in response to Request for Tender (RFT) 13016 to provide research leadership and management services for the Operational Energy Transitions Defence Research Centre (OET DRC).
Defence Innovation, Science and Technology Strategy 2026 (DISTS 26) calls for Defence to progress the formation of DRCs in partnership with universities and industry to focus on enduring and complex IS&T priorities that require interdisciplinary teams.
The OET DRC is a response to a fundamental shift in the role of energy within Defence capability and operations. It is intended to provide Defence with a scalable and enduring mechanism to shape the Defence energy landscape and deliver operationally relevant, deployable energy solutions that support the future Integrated Force
The OET DRC will operate as a problem-led, outcome-focused enterprise, integrating Defence, academia, industry and international partners into a coherent, mission-driven effort. Its role is not to conduct isolated, exploratory or basic research, but to accelerate the adoption, integration, and transition of energy technologies into deployable Defence capability, particularly where conventional market or program mechanisms are insufficient.

title: ANSTO Emergency Services Response Team (ERT) Services Registration of Interest (ROI)
description:
The Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO) invites suitably qualified and experienced suppliers to submit a Registration of Interest (ROI) for the provision of Emergency Services Response Team (ERT) Services at its Lucas Heights campus in New South Wales.
ANSTO is seeking a supplier capable of providing an integrated emergency response capability supporting ANSTO's emergency preparedness and response arrangements. The Emergency Services Response Team (ERT) performs a critical role in supporting the safety and resilience of ANSTO's operations and is responsible for emergency medical response, fire response, hazardous materials response, emergency preparedness activities and incident support services.
The successful supplier will be expected to demonstrate strong operational capability, workforce flexibility, emergency response expertise, effective training and competency management arrangements and a commitment to continuous improvement while supporting ANSTO's core values of safety, security and sustainability.
Given the nature of ANSTO's operations and the sensitivity of information relevant to this procurement, access to detailed Request for Tender (RFT) documentation will be restricted.
The purpose of this ROI is to:
• Identify suppliers with the capability, capacity and relevant experience to perform the Services;
• Confirm suppliers satisfy the minimum participation requirements;
• Establish suppliers willing to comply with ANSTO's confidentiality and probity requirements; and
• Determine which suppliers will be invited to participate in the subsequent RFT process.
As part of the ROI process, suppliers will be required to:
• Complete and submit the ROI Response Schedules;
• Execute ANSTO's Confidentiality Deed;
• Demonstrate compliance with the minimum participation requirements specified in the ATM documentation.
Following evaluation of ROI submissions, ANSTO intends to shortlist suppliers that satisfy the ROI requirements and invite those suppliers to participate in Stage Two, being the Request for Tender.

title: Private Hospital Services
description:
DVA is seeking the provision of Private Hospital services for Entitled Persons by publishing this Invitation to Provide Private Hospital Services to the Veteran Community.
DVA serves Australia’s veteran community, through the provision of programmes of care, compensation and commemoration.
DVA’s aim is to secure high quality private hospital care for Entitled Persons delivered for a fair price, at the most convenient locations for Entitled Persons. As the veteran community ages, their capacity to access a wider range of care appropriate to their needs is increasingly important. Managing emerging and different needs of contemporary veterans is also a priority. DVA also aims to continually improve the quality and safety of services, and the health outcomes for DVA clients, through the purchase of evidence-based treatment services.
DVA’s New Approach to Contracting for Private Hospital Services
In the past DVA contracted with Private Hospitals for services to Entitled Persons through a Request for Tenders (RFT).
The current process that DVA is engaging in with Private Hospital providers is not an RFT.
DVA has introduced new arrangements for providers to contract with DVA. This is a simplified contracting model that DVA is using to facilitate engagement with suitably qualified providers.
A summary of the key features of the new arrangements are:
maximising the numbers of participating providers to achieve wide access to private hospitals services for the veteran community;
there is no competition, all qualified providers can participate;
while providers are required to submit the fee tables, there is no requirement for tender submission or evaluation of tenders;
providers self-certify their compliance with DVA’s terms and conditions of the Hospital Services Agreement;
providers can enter into the Hospital Services Agreement at any time and the Hospital Services Agreement will continue until DVA ends the arrangements or the Contracting Entity exits the arrangements with DVA; and
negotiation only on fees to ensure value for money.

The OET DRC is being developed in response to a fundamental shift in the role of energy within Defence capability and operations. Energy is no longer a background enabler, but a central determinant of operational effectiveness, underpinning operational tempo, persistence, survivability, and freedom of action in increasingly contested and degraded environments.
To support the establishment of the OET DRC and the delivery of its Inaugural Research Projects (IRPs), the Commonwealth is undertaking two separate but related processes in parallel as follows:
1. ATM ID 13016 Lead Partner Request For Tender (RFT) (separate process): to engage a supplier as a Lead Partner to provide research leadership and expertise at the program and project level for the OET DRC; and
2. ATM ID 13457 Contributing Partner Request For Information (RFI) (this RFI): to engage with the market for the purposes of:
- understanding market capability and potential suppliers that align with, and have interest in, research related to the OET DRC Themes; and
- informing the development and conduct of other procurement processes (including future procurement processes).
This RFI is separate from the Lead Partner RFT process. Further information regarding the Lead Partner RFT can be found on AusTender under ATM ID 13016.
The OET DRC will initially address the following five areas (OET DRC Themes):
1. Dispersed Energy Access at the Tactical Edge
2. Sustainment Under Contested Conditions
3. Resilient and Scalable Forward Energy Systems
4. Enabling Next-Generation High-Power and High-Consumption Capabilities
5. Extended Endurance and Reduced Logistic Dependence
Defence’s overall objective is to support innovative, low Technology Readiness Level research that advances new knowledge, develops emerging concepts or prototypes and has the potential to contribute to future capability outcomes associated with the OET DRC Themes.
This RFI invites entities interested in the OET DRC Themes to provide a response that outlines their research expertise, capability and facilities. Respondents are also invited to put forward unique or novel research and technology approaches to enable practical solutions under the OET DRC Themes.

title: EOI - Supply of Direct Drive Chiller
description:
The Australian Synchrotron (AS) is a world-class research facility operated by the Australian Nuclear Science and Technology Organisation (ANSTO) at Clayton, Victoria. The facility operates continuously and relies on a central refrigeration system to provide chilled water for critical facility heat loads, including low-conductivity water (LCW) cooling and HVAC systems.
Chiller 1 is one of four chillers serving the primary cooling circuit. It is approximately 22 years old, has accumulated significant run hours and has reached end of life, with spare parts no longer readily available. Replacement is required to restore reliable N+1 cooling redundancy and reduce the risk of loss of critical cooling capacity.
The existing system supplies chilled water at approximately 6°C, with return water at approximately 10°C. The condenser water circuit typically enters the chiller at approximately 20°C and leaves at approximately 23°C for heat rejection through the cooling towers.

title: Notice of RFT - Refresh and Expansion of the Professions of the Panel of Outreach Program Counsellors for the
description:
This is a pre-release notice to provide advance notification of a proposed RFT for the Refresh and Expansion of the Professions of the Panel.
Please note, eligibility, application requirements, assessment processes, and contractual arrangements will be set out in the forthcoming RFT. No evaluation criteria, scoring methodology, or commercial terms are being released at this stage. The Department reserves the right to modify or cancel the proposed RFT at its discretion.
Background on Open Arms
Open Arms is Australia’s national accredited provider of mental health and wellbeing services for veterans and the families of veterans.
Open Arms provides mental health counselling, relationship counselling, peer support services, and group programs for people with Australian Defence Force (ADF) service (current and former serving members) and their immediate families.
Open Arms provides free and confidential counselling through a national network of multidisciplinary mental health professionals, delivered in dedicated Open Arms centres by the DVA’s staff, or through the Panel; being a network of accredited mental health clinicians, engaged to support the delivery of services on behalf of Open Arms across Australia through the Outreach Program.
Open Arms can provide counselling, care coordination and peer support services to veterans and the families of veterans within an episode of care model, where clients engage with our services for goal directed interventions for a defined period.
Open Arms aims to provide timely access to appropriate services and care, based on a comprehensive holistic assessment and integrated care pathways to meet client needs and support recovery. This includes working in partnership with health systems, including primary health, as well as other community agencies to ensure comprehensive support for our clients.
Background on the Panel and Outreach Program
Open Arms’ Model of Care provides the organisational framework that underpins the delivery of all Outreach Program services. It guides how we support veterans and the families of veterans through trauma-informed, military-aware, recovery-oriented care, while ensuring consistent clinical governance, quality service delivery and positive client outcomes. In 2024 the Panel was established through which Outreach Providers provide Open Arms services to clients. The Panel is the mechanism for Open Arms to engage with Outreach Providers to ensure the highest level of support can be delivered to clients. Only organisations or individuals appointed to the Panel can provide Open Arms Outreach Program Counselling Services.
The categories of services that are delivered through the Panel include:
Outreach Program Counsellors (OPCs), who provide individual, couples, or family counselling
Group Program Facilitators (GPFs), who facilitate evidence-informed, military-aware group programs that strengthen resilience, build practical skills, and promote wellbeing
Clinical Supervisors, who provide professional supervision to Open Arms’ staff.
Outreach Providers on the Panel can provide one, two or all three service streams, depending on their qualifications, experience and the services they are approved to deliver.
Go to the Open Arms website for further information:
https://www.openarms.gov.au/about/open-arms-outreach-program
Expansion of definition of OPC
In 2025 the Veterans’ Entitlements (Treatment Principles) Amendment (Outreach Program Counsellor) Determination 2025 and the Military Rehabilitation and Compensation (Treatment Principles) Amendment (Outreach Program Counsellor) Determination 2025), were enacted which amended the MRCA Treatment Principles (No. MRCC 53/2013) and the Treatment Principles (Instrument 2013 No. R52) – (collectively the Treatment Principles) – to expand the types of professions who can provide Outreach Program Counselling as an Outreach Program Counsellor (OPC). Now that occupational therapists, registered nurses, social workers (general) and counsellors are recognised as additional profession types eligible to apply to become a provider, the Department wishes to update the Panel accordingly through the proposed RFT.
The Department is therefore looking to procure Outreach Providers from the following eligible professions:
a person who is registered with AHPRA as a psychologist;
a person who is registered with AHPRA as an occupational therapist;
a person who is registered with AHPRA as a registered nurse;
a person who is eligible for membership with the Australian Association of Social Workers;
or
a person who is registered:
as a registered clinical counsellor with the Psychotherapy and Counselling Federation of Australia;
as a counsellor at registration category Level 3 or Level 4 with the Australian Counselling Association Limited.
The Department is currently planning to release the RFT to market through publication on AusTender in September 2026, however this timeframe may be subject to change.
Please note that this is not an RFT and does not commit the Department to proceed. The Close Date and Time stated in this notice relates to this pre-release notice only and does not reflect the proposed RFT commencement and closing dates for potential tenderers to lodge their submissions. The RFT, where undertaken, will be published on AusTender and will include the Closing Date and Time for lodgement of submissions.

title: Navy Way Point Leadership Program
description:
Navy Training Authority Initial Training Leadership and Management (TA-ITLM) requires a suitably qualified Supplier to develop and deliver the Navy Way Point program. The program is designed to complement the current Navy Senior Leadership Program (NSLP) and other existing career professional development offerings.
In order to provide a more career-focused professional development opportunity for Captains, particularly those who are new to the Canberra environment, Navy is seeking a reality-based program with a focus on participant interaction, containing practical exercises based on real world scenarios.
The aim of the Way Point Program is to develop the ability of selected senior officers to comprehend the strategic environment and to provide influential, Joint and Whole of Australian Government (WoAG) options that support Government strategic objectives. The course should develop participants' strategic comprehension, thinking and communication skills, and the behaviours and attitudes needed to be effective as a commander or senior staff officer in a Joint, Defence and WoAG team.
The program should include a broad range of highly experienced presenters from across the national security spectrum, with the intent to provide officers new to the Canberra environment, with the skills and confidence operating with influence in Joint, Defence, WoAG and international environments.
Each Navy Way Point program shall be five (5) days in length for up to 24 participants. Taking place in Canberra once per calendar year, with delivery in Q2 (April-June).

The scope, however, refers to integration with Content Manager, and the Shire expects its own IT staff to build integrations to retained systems. A single platform that holds records and ERP transactions together would remove an interface, reduce ongoing integration effort for the Shire, and place accountability for records compliance and migration with one provider. Please confirm that respondents may propose replacement of Content Manager as part of the core solution, and that a replacement proposal will be evaluated on the same basis as an integration approach under the Fit for Purpose criterion. If so, please advise: (a) whether migration of existing records, metadata and retention and disposal information is in scope; (b) the approximate volume (record count and storage size); (c) whether replacement may be priced as an option alongside integration; and (d) whether a replacement solution may be hosted within the Shire's existing Microsoft 365 tenant.

2. Staff and user numbers (Sections 2.2.1 and 2.2.2, Annexure C) Section 2.2.1 states 225 employees including 58 casual staff, Section 2.2.2 states approximately 165 permanent and 60 casual staff, and Annexure C refers to approximately 200 staff and 51 casual staff. publicQuestions.answer:
Q1 Records Management & Content Manager

•	Respondents may propose native records management in place of Content Manager. Both approaches will be evaluated on the same basis under Fit for Purpose. Any replacement must meet the State Records Act 2000 and the Shire’s Recordkeeping Plan.

(a)	Yes. Migration of existing records, metadata and retention and disposal information is in scope where replacement is proposed.

(b)	Volumes are [TBC]. Respondents should state their assumed volumes in Annexure C.

(c)	Yes. Price replacement in the Records Management lines of Annexure C and show the integration-only cost separately in the Assumptions / Notes column.

(d)	Yes. Respondents should state any Microsoft 365 licensing or configuration dependencies.

Q2 Submission Format & Order

•	Annexures A, B and C are to be submitted in Excel, together with the PDF version of the RFT document. Scanned pages signed in wet ink are acceptable; pasted, typed or initialled signatures are not. Supplementary documentation is to be placed last.

Q3 Staff Numbers & Users

•	Total employees – 225 (60 of which are casual)

•	Full ERP access – 10

•	Limited ERP access – 100

•	Kiosk access – 225

Q4 Price Basis

•	Respondents may apply an annual adjustment to recurring subscription, licensing and support fees. Implementation costs remain fixed lump sum. Respondents must state the following in the Annual Price Adjustment section of Annexure C.

*whether an adjustment applies

*the basis of the adjustment (fixed percentage, CPI or other)

*any rate or cap

*the first adjustment date

Q5 Contract Term

•	Pricing is required for the initial five (5) year term, as set out in the Annexure C Costs Summary.

Q6 Alternative Response

•	Departures to the standard SaaS agreement listed in Section 5.7 (List of Contract Departures Requested) will be treated as part of a conforming response, and the response does not need to be marked as an Alternative Response.

Q7 Asset Management

•	Asset management is seen as an optional module and forms part of Annexure B

Q8 Leisure Centre & HR Integration

•	MALC staff are included in the 225 staff count for payroll, rostering & timesheets

•	Integration with Pulse (HR) software not a mandatory function but worth noting if readily available

Q9 Data Migration

•	The extent of data migration is yet to be determined and agreed with the successful vendor. Please provide an hourly rate at Section 5.5 if your solution offers assistance with data migration.

Q10 Award Timing

•	We anticipate a decision being made by Council by no later than May 2027.

Q11 Requirement Priorities

•	INF-037	Should be a “SHOULD”

•	CRM-019	Should be a “MUST” but the requirement should read “The system should identify a duplicate record and allow the user to accept or merge the record”.

•	CRM-031	Should be a “MUST”

•	INF-021	Should be a “SHOULD”

•	INF-051	Ignore INF-051

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Wingham Sports Complex is an established community sporting facility servicing rugby league, touch football and soccer, including junior and senior training and competition activities.

Fields 3 and 4 are the primary illuminated playing fields within the complex and are currently serviced by six existing 20 m sports lighting poles fitted with metal-halide floodlights. The existing lighting infrastructure is approximately 20 years old and Council is seeking to upgrade the system to modern LED sports lighting to improve lighting performance, reliability, energy efficiency and ongoing maintenance outcomes.

Field 5 is located immediately north of Fields 3 and 4 and is currently used predominantly as an overflow field for junior sport and training. The field does not currently have sufficient sports lighting to support regular night-time use. With increasing participation across the resident sporting codes, Council has identified the need to increase the usable capacity of the complex by providing compliant sports lighting to Field 5.

The proposed works will extend lighting coverage to Field 5 through the installation of two new sports lighting poles along the northern side of the field and the utilisation of existing lighting poles on the southern side. Council is also considering the broader replacement of the existing metal-halide lighting servicing Fields 3 and 4 as part of the project.

The completed lighting system is intended to achieve a minimum maintained average horizontal illuminance of 100 lux across the nominated playing areas, providing suitable lighting for evening training and community-level sporting use while improving the overall capacity and flexibility of Wingham Sports Complex.

title: Call for Expressions of Interest: System Restart Service (SWIS-wide)
description:
AEMO is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) to understand the availability, location and readiness of Facilities that may be able to provide System Restart Service across the SWIS.

Previous System Restart Service engagements have indicated that other existing or new Facilities may also be capable of providing System Restart Service, subject to necessary site works, testing and lead times.

AEMO invites Market Participants, or prospective Market Participants, with Facilities capable of providing System Restart Service to make submissions for:

* a Facility with System Restart Service capability to commence from 23 October 2028 (EOI Part 1); and

* a Facility with System Restart Service capability to commence only after October 2030 (EOI Part 2).

AEMO welcomes submissions for either existing or proposed Facilities with different technology configurations to submit an EOI. The EOI will be used by AEMO to determine the requirements of a subsequent tender, such as the location of the service (Sub-Network) and service commencement period.

AEMO will specifically use the information from the EOI to:

* identify a short-list of candidates that are able to meet the System Restart Standard;

* assess the efficacy to provide System Restart Services;

* review and potentially amend the System Restart Standard, including the Electrical Sub-Network boundaries (i.e. this is to determine the location AEMO will be tendering for the System Restart Service); and

* confirm with short-listed candidates any necessary upgrades or capital works to be compliant with the future System Restart Standard and the System Restart Service Specification and identify associated timelines to provide the service.

All submissions:

* must be provided in good faith but are not binding on the respondent; and

* will be treated as confidential information under applicable Electricity System and Market Rules.

Submissions must be provided via VendorPanel in accordance with the EOI Guideline by 5pm AWST on 9 November 2026.

publicQuestions.question:
Please confirm if existing bathrooms are to be ‘renovated’ as annotated on drawing no. CD2

publicQuestions.answer:
Please find our response to the queries below:

1. Please confirm if existing bathrooms are to be ‘renovated’ as annotated on drawing no. CD2:

The existing bathroom facilities are to receive a general cosmetic refresh as part of the project. The Contractor shall allow for:

•	Repainting of existing walls and ceilings, where applicable.

•	General cleaning and tidying of existing bathroom areas.

•	Minor cosmetic touch-ups to existing finishes.

•	Making good of surfaces affected by the refurbishment works.

The existing bathroom layout, fixtures, fittings and services are generally to be retained. The scope is limited to a cosmetic refresh and does not require a complete bathroom renovation.

2. Please advise if continuation of architectural finishes such as the slat style ceiling finish to the departure’s terminal is required, or if we are to allow new throughout:

The existing slat-style ceiling finish within the departure terminal is not required to be continued throughout the upgraded terminal.

The design intent is to achieve a clean, simple and modern appearance without requiring a new ceiling finish throughout the proposed extension and refurbishment areas.

However, the Contractor shall include a provisional sum for the supply and installation of a slat-style ceiling finish throughout the proposed areas as an alternative for Council's consideration.

The Contractor shall provide details of the proposed slat-style ceiling finish, including materials, profiles and colours, for Council's review and approval during the design development stage.

The proposed new skylights identified on Drawing CD2 are not required.

The Contractor shall exclude the provision of new skylights from the proposed works and allow for the continuous roof construction in accordance with the revised architectural design requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
Airport terminal tender RFI questions

Wagga Wagga Airport Terminal Upgrade

Contract CT2027017 30 October 2026

Please clarify the following items so tenderers can establish consistent allowances for scope, design and operational requirements.

References below use the issued PPR, Design Requirements, concept drawings and furniture schedule. NCC clause references are to NCC 2022 Volume One, subject to confirmation under RFI 001.

RFI 001 Applicable NCC edition and certification pathway

The PPR refers to the NCC latest edition. Please confirm the NCC edition and referenced standards tenderers are to adopt, including whether Council requires NCC 2025 before its statutory adoption in NSW. Please confirm the building certification pathway under the proposed Part 5 approval process and how the applicable edition will be fixed for the project.

Reference: PPR Standards and Quality, page 10, and Certification, page 24.

RFI 002 Existing building compliance and fire safety records

Please provide available BCA assessments, approved building classifications, fire engineering reports, fire safety schedules and existing evacuation plans. Please identify known deficiencies and clarify the intended extent of upgrades to retained areas outside the alterations shown on the concept drawings.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 12, page 17. PPR Fire Services, page 26. NCC Sections C, D and E.

RFI 003 Passenger numbers and operational design criteria

Please provide the required peak simultaneous arriving and departing passenger numbers, accompanying visitors, staff numbers and anticipated flight overlap. Please distinguish the minimum seating capacity from total design occupancy and identify any future passenger growth allowance required for terminal planning and building services.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 10, 13 and 18. NCC D2D18 and Part F4.

RFI 004 Existing amenities refurbishment and layout changes

CD2 identifies refurbishment of the existing amenities. Please confirm the extent of replacement of finishes, partitions, fixtures and services. Where compliant access or cubicle clearances require changes to the footprint or adjoining spaces, will Council accept those changes, subject to structural assessment of walls supporting the existing plant slab?

Reference: CD2. Design Requirements Section 22, page 34. NCC F4D5, F4D8 and Part I2.

RFI 005 Accessible adult change facility

Please identify any existing accessible adult change facility available to serve the terminal and confirm the preferred location for a new facility where required, including acceptance of associated layout changes. The supplied concept and furniture schedule identify a parents room and baby change station but do not identify an adult change facility.

Reference: CD2. Furniture Schedule FIX-05. NCC F4D12(1)(e) and Specification 27.

 RFI 006 Airside emergency egress

Please provide the existing approved airside evacuation arrangements and identify the routes, perimeter gates and assembly areas available to serve the upgraded terminal. Please confirm airport security restrictions affecting emergency gate operation, including any required fire alarm or access control interfaces.

Reference: PPR Emergency and Evacuation Plan, page 22. NCC D2D15 and D3D26.

RFI 007 Water supply pressure and flow testing

Please provide a current water authority statement of available pressure and flow, together with site pressure and flow test results representative of the proposed fire service connection. Results should identify the test location and date, static pressure, residual pressures and corresponding flow rates, and any supply limitations. If current results are unavailable, please arrange testing before tender close. We have experienced low water pressure on other works in the area and need this information to assess potential fire water storage, pumps or supply upgrades. Please also provide records of existing fire water infrastructure available to serve the terminal.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 9 and 12. NCC E1D2 and AS 2419.1. FRNSW Hydraulic fire safety system design position statement.

RFI 008 Retained glazing and Section J upgrade scope

Please provide any existing energy assessment and clarify the required treatment of retained glazing and building fabric where existing and new spaces are combined. Please confirm the scope boundary for upgrades identified by the contractor's Section J assessment, including retained departure lounge glazing and areas outside the highlighted refurbishment footprint.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 10 and 23. PPR Sustainability, page 29. NCC Section J.

RFI 009 Mechanical coverage and performance requirements

Section 10 requires new reverse cycle heating and cooling throughout the entire terminal. Please provide Council's required indoor design conditions, operating hours and zoning criteria, including the front waiting area, cafe, baggage collection and exit areas. Please identify any spaces intended to remain unconditioned and requirements associated with frequently opening external doors.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 10, pages 13 and 14. PPR Mechanical, pages 26 and 27.

RFI 010 Alternative heating solutions

Would Council consider hydronic or radiant heating as a supplement to, or a separately priced alternative to, the specified reverse cycle arrangement? Please confirm the acceptance criteria and tender presentation requirements for any alternative proposed to address the high internal spaces and intermittent terminal occupancy.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 10. PPR Value for Money, page 20.

 RFI 011 Plant room location discrepancy

Please reconcile the plant room shown on CD2 and the north elevation on CD3 around grids 6 and 7 with Section EE on CD4, which shows plant above the parents room and cafeteria around grids 5 and 6. Please confirm any mandatory location or slab requirement and whether alternative engineered support arrangements may be proposed.

Reference: CD2, CD3 and CD4 Section EE. Design Requirements Section 22, page 34.

RFI 012 Plant access and external openings

Please arrange tender inspection access to the plant rooms and equipment that could not be accessed during the site visit. Please identify restrictions on introducing external louvres, maintenance openings or temporary openings for plant removal and replacement, and any plant access routes that must remain available throughout construction.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 10, 22 and 24. PPR Roof and Other High Level Access, page 21.

RFI 013 Existing structural drawings and investigation records

Please provide the 1984 and 2007 existing airport drawings referenced in the PPR attachments, together with any available original structural calculations and historical geotechnical records, including records held by the original structural engineer. We note that no geotechnical report has been issued and that existing information requires verification by the contractor.

Reference: PPR Site Information, pages 13 and 14, and Section 7 Attachments. Design Requirements Sections 2, 3 and 7.

RFI 014 Electrical supply capacity and upgrade boundaries

Please provide available electrical single line diagrams, switchboard schedules, supply capacity information and relevant authority correspondence. Please confirm the geographical extent of incoming supply upgrades to be included, including any upstream network works, and identify known supply authority restrictions or required upgrades relevant to the proposed terminal loads.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 11, page 15. PPR Electrical, page 25.

RFI 015 Stormwater infrastructure and drainage constraints

Please provide existing drainage surveys and records showing pipe sizes, levels, pits and outfalls around the road and proposed extension. Please identify infrastructure that must remain in position, approved discharge points, and restrictions on diversions or road excavation. Please confirm any mandatory constraints affecting roof drainage connections and overflow discharge locations.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 8, page 11. PPR Civil and Roof Drainage, pages 24 and 25.

 RFI 016 Cafe scope and retained fitout

Section 19 states that the cafe is to remain generally unchanged. Please confirm whether Council requires any cafe fitout or equipment work beyond the specified replacement furniture, protection and necessary service interfaces. Please identify additional requirements arising from the existing lease or cafe operator, including any nominated future tenancy works.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 19 and 20. Furniture Schedule DEP-04.

RFI 017 Furniture quantities and charging positions

Please confirm whether the minimum 160 departure seats, 20 table or stool or chair positions, 20 working bench positions, four modular or booth sets and four cafe sets are separate cumulative requirements. Please nominate seats per booth set and chairs per cafe set, and confirm the required overall seating capacity. Please confirm the charging requirements for each relevant furniture group.

Reference: Furniture Schedule DEP-02 to DEP-06. Design Requirements Sections 20.2, 20.3 and 20.5.

RFI 018 Screening equipment and passenger recomposure facilities

Please provide the Council supplied screening equipment schedule, layouts, service requirements, installation clearances and delivery dates. Please confirm responsibility for equipment installation and commissioning. Please also confirm the required quantity and arrangement of seating and benches immediately after screening for passengers to replace footwear and repack belongings.

Reference: Design Requirements Section 14, pages 20 and 21, and Section 18, page 26.

RFI 019 Aboriginal artwork and relocation requirements

Section 20.4 requires retention or relocation of existing artwork glazing, while CD2 identifies cladding with Indigenous artwork. Please confirm whether the cladding incorporates relocated artwork, reproduction of existing images or newly commissioned artwork. Please provide the required extent, relocation destination and approval arrangements, including any restrictions on removal or temporary storage.

Reference: CD2. Design Requirements Section 20.4, page 29.

RFI 020 Curved roof barge and external door requirements

Please confirm any mandatory architectural requirements for the curved roof barge, including whether a continuous rolled finish is required or segmented construction is acceptable. Please also identify any nominated external door construction, or confirm that durable metal faced or metal clad doors may be proposed through design development.

Reference: CD3 and CD4. Design Requirements Sections 5, 20 and 23.

RFI 021 Operational staging and service changeovers

Please provide operational restrictions relevant to staging, including minimum passenger facilities, permitted service shutdown windows, cafe continuity requirements and notice periods. Please identify constraints affecting mechanical plant removal, temporary heating and cooling, and retention of existing walls until later construction stages. Please confirm the process and review periods for approving these arrangements.

Reference: Design Requirements Sections 6, 24 and 25. PPR Contractor's Program and Emergency and Evacuation Plan.

publicQuestions.question:
What is the council’s required timeframe for completion?

Please advise of the physical security requirements for the building including elements such as wall construction specification, wall heights, glass specifications etc.
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Required Timeframe for Completion

Council has not specified a separate timeframe for completion. The Contractor shall develop and submit a detailed program identifying the proposed design, approvals, construction, testing, commissioning and handover activities, with completion in accordance with the submitted and approved program and the Contract requirements.

2.	Physical Security Requirements

The Contractor shall provide physical security measures appropriate for the Airport Terminal, in accordance with the RFT requirements, applicable aviation security legislation, the Airport Operator's security requirements and the National Construction Code (NCC).

The RFT does not prescribe specific wall construction specifications, minimum wall heights or security glazing specifications. These shall be determined by the Contractor as part of the detailed design, taking into consideration the security requirements of the building and the separation between public, staff and security-controlled areas.

Glazing shall comply with the applicable NCC requirements and relevant Australian Standards, including AS 1288 (Glass in buildings – Selection and installation) and AS 2047 (Windows and external glazed doors in buildings), as applicable.

The Contractor shall submit the proposed wall, door and glazing specifications and associated security arrangements to Council and the Airport Operator for review and approval.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

Please see below RFIs:

Can you please confirm the scope of works to occur within the 'Cafe/Caffeteria' space?

Are there any height restrictions/requirements for crane operations during construction?

Can you please confirm the number of seats that need to be supplied for the 'Departure Lounges'. There is a quantity of 378 shown in the concept drawings which conflicts with the 160 listed on the Furniture & Finishes Schedule.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The existing café area within the Airport Terminal is to remain generally unchanged as part of the project.

The Contractor shall allow for protection of the existing cafe fitout and equipment, together with coordination of any necessary building services interfaces associated with the Works.

No additional cafe fitout or equipment replacement is required beyond the documented scope. Any works arising from the existing cafe lease or operator requirements that are not identified in the RFT documentation shall be referred to Council for direction.

2. No specific maximum crane height.

The Contractor shall coordinate all crane and lifting operations with Council and the Airport Operator before commencement. The Contractor shall submit a crane and lifting plan identifying the proposed crane location and configuration, date and duration, maximum crane height, operating radius and potential impacts on aircraft operations, passenger movements, airport access, security and emergency access.

All required approvals must be obtained before crane operations commence. Operations shall only occur during approved hours. Any operation outside approved hours requires prior approval from Council and the Airport Operator.

3. The concept drawings are provided for reference purposes only. The Contractor shall allow for the supply and installation of all seating and furniture in accordance with the quantities specified in the Finishes and Furniture Schedule.

The quantities identified in the Finishes and Furniture Schedule are separate requirements and shall be allowed for cumulatively, as follows:

DEP-02: 160 individual Departure Lounge seats.

DEP-03: 20 table/stool/chair positions.

DEP-04: Four café furniture sets.

DEP-05: 20 working bench positions.

DEP-06: Four modular/booth seating sets.

The quantity of 378 seats shown on the concept drawings is indicative only and does not override the quantities specified in the Finishes and Furniture Schedule.

The Contractor shall develop the final furniture layout and propose the number of seats within each booth and cafe furniture set, ensuring adequate passenger circulation and accessible paths of travel, for Council's review and approval.

description:
The Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) invites responses to this Request for Information (RFI) from suppliers of technology products, platforms, data, integration and related services that may support the Transport Coordination Centre (TCC).

The Transport Coordination Centre (TCC) Program is a multi-year TMR transformation initiative to establish a statewide, integrated, multi-modal transport coordination facility and operating model.

TMR will lead the TCC as a multi-modal operations centre that integrates Queensland’s key transport modes, including road, rail, bus, light rail and ferry.

The TCC will oversee real-time network management, optimisation, disruption response, customer communications, demand management, data analysis and performance reporting. Its vision is to enable safer, smoother and more reliable travel for passengers and freight across Queensland through reduced travel times, improved journey reliability, faster incident response, personalised updates, increased freight efficiency and more efficient use of existing transport infrastructure.

The TCC will be established before the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games and will scale to manage Games-time transport demand.

The TCC Program has multiple delivery streams. This RFI is issued by the Technology stream and relates to the operational systems, platforms, data and enabling technology required for the TCC to deliver its services.

title: Cairns Marine Precinct - Common User Facility (CMP-CUF) Co-Investment
description:
The Opportunity:

Ports North is pleased to advise that Request for Proposal (RFP) Phase 1 for the Cairns Marine Precinct - Common User Facility (CMP-CUF) Co-Investment Opportunity has now commenced.

Ports North is proposing the development of the Cairns Marine Precinct – Common User Facility, a major maritime infrastructure project, to expand the marine vessel maintenance capability and capacity in Far North Queensland to support the continued growth of the region’s maritime industry. The proposed facility responds to increasing demand for maritime maintenance, repair, and overhaul services as global vessel fleets expand and age, alongside sustained investment in Australia’s maritime defence capability driving long-term sustainment demand.

Ports North has identified a Finance (co-funded), Design, Build, Operate and Maintain (FDBOM) commercial delivery model as the most efficient means of Project delivery to successfully facilitate achievement of the Project Objectives. As the Project will benefit from a significant contribution of funds from the Queensland and Commonwealth Governments, the physical facilities coming into existence as a result of the Project will be a common user facility available for use by the operator and customers including vessel owners and ship maintenance and repair service providers.

Ports North is seeking a private sector proponent to co-fund, develop, operate and maintain the facility under a long-term arrangement on Ports North-owned land at the Port of Cairns.

This RFP follows the successful completion of an Expression of Interest (EOI) process. Participation in the EOI process was not a prerequisite for participation in RFP Phase 1. Ports North welcomes registrations and proposals from organisations that did not participate in the EOI and may be engaging with the opportunity for the first time.

Purpose of this Request for Proposal:

The purpose of this RFP is to elicit proposals from the market that address the Project Objectives and develop the CMP-CUF, including the following:

•	the co-funding of the Project;

•	the design, construction and commissioning of the CMP-CUF; and

•	the operation and maintenance of the CMP-CUF on a common user basis.

How to Participate in RFP Phase 1:

Proposals are being accepted only via the Ansarada CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room. Submissions via this Queensland Procurement Solution may not be eligible.

To participate:

- register online via https://www.portsnorth.com.au/ports-north-projects/cairns-marine-precinct

- Shortly after, Ports North will provide access to the Ansarada CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room

- Access the RFP documentation within the CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room

- Submit your RFP via the CMP-CUF RFP Phase 1 Data Room prior to 1200 AEST on Friday 18 December 2026.

Enquiries regarding the procurement process may be directed to cmpenquiry@portsnorth.com.au.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi, can you advise on what basis the previous valuation was conducted (i.e. cost approach, market approach or income approach) and whether the other approaches were tested to ensure the correct approach was chosen? This is asked because waste facilities can have significant market value depending on the attributes of the facility and thereby determine the correct valuation approach.

This question is asked because the specification calls on the provider to build on the previous valuation, and it would be nice to know if the previous valuation was fully tested and the correct approach used.
publicQuestions.answer:
The Muswellbrook Waste Facility valuation as at 30 June 2024 used the cost approach. As documented in Section 6, page 19 of the amended Talis final report, Talis adopted the replacement cost method using Level 3 inputs, citing restrictions on the disposal of public infrastructure and the absence of an identifiable market. Talis reviewed a site-specific construction estimate from a local contractor and checked the replacement cost rates against other industry data.

The available records do not document separate testing of the market or income approaches.

The 2024 valuation and its supporting information provide a starting point for the 30 June 2027 revaluation. The appointed valuer is to independently determine and document the most appropriate valuation approach, taking into account the facility’s characteristics and the evidence available at the valuation date, including any relevant market or income evidence.

title: Whitsunday Regional Sports Precinct Stage 1 - Design and Construction
description:
The Whitsunday Regional Council (Principal) is delivering the Whitsunday Regional Sports Precinct (WRSP) to address the increasing demand for high-quality sporting, recreation and community infrastructure across the Whitsunday Region.

The WRSP is one of Council's most significant community infrastructure investments and will provide a contemporary regional sporting destination that supports organised sport, community participation, recreation, health and wellbeing, regional events and long-term population growth. The precinct has been planned to meet current community needs while providing a scalable framework for future expansion through subsequent stages of development.

Stage 1 represents the first phase of the Master Plan and will establish the core sporting facilities, supporting infrastructure and services required to enable the precinct to operate as a high-quality regional sports hub. The completed works are intended to provide durable, functional and maintainable infrastructure that delivers value for money over the life of the asset while supporting a broad range of community users.

This Principal's Project Requirements (PPR) defines the minimum functional, operational, technical and performance requirements for the Project. It establishes the outcomes that the Contractor is required to achieve and forms the basis upon which the Contractor will develop, coordinate, design, construct, commission and hand over the Works.

The Works will be delivered under an AS 4300–1995 Design and Construct Contract, under which the Contractor will assume full responsibility for the detailed design, design coordination, statutory approvals, construction, commissioning, testing and handover of the completed facility, except where expressly stated otherwise in the Contract.

This Project is funded under the Australian Government Growing Regions Program. In accordance with the Project Funding Agreement, the Head Contractor must hold and maintain current accreditation under the Australian Government Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme (the Scheme) for the entirety of the Contract.

Tenderers must:

a)	hold current accreditation under the Australian Government Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme at the Tender Closing Time;

b)	provide evidence of current accreditation with their Tender submission;

c)	maintain accreditation for the duration of the Contract, including any extensions of time or defects liability period where accreditation is required to remain in force; and

d)	immediately notify the Principal of any actual or proposed suspension, lapse, cancellation or variation to their accreditation status.

A non-mandatory Tender Site Briefing will be held on Tuesday, 6 October 2026, 1.30 pm (AEST). The location of the meeting will commence at Proserpine Administration Building, 83-85 Main Street, Proserpine Qld 4800 and will progress to the Site Visit at Shute Harbour Road and Brandy Creek Road. Access to the Site is adjacent to the bus stop pair refer to the Conditions of Tender clause 7 for a map for parking at the Site.

N.B. PPE is a requirement to attend this site, at a minimum Hi-Vis long-sleeved shirt, full length pants, steel cap boots and eye protection, it is also recommended to wear sun protection.

Please confirm your attendance at this meeting via contracts@whitsundayrc.qld.gov.au no later than midday, Thursday, 1 October 2026.

All communications must go through the VendorPanel communications forum.

The Whitsunday Regional Council (Principal) is delivering the Whitsunday Regional Sports Precinct (WRSP) to address the increasing demand for high-quality sporting, recreation and community infrastructure across the Whitsunday Region.

The WRSP is one of Council's most significant community infrastructure investments and will provide a contemporary regional sporting destination that supports organised sport, community participation, recreation, health and wellbeing, regional events and long-term population growth. The precinct has been planned to meet current community needs while providing a scalable framework for future expansion through subsequent stages of development.

Stage 1 represents the first phase of the Master Plan and will establish the core sporting facilities, supporting infrastructure and services required to enable the precinct to operate as a high-quality regional sports hub. The completed works are intended to provide durable, functional and maintainable infrastructure that delivers value for money over the life of the asset while supporting a broad range of community users.

This Principal's Project Requirements (PPR) defines the minimum functional, operational, technical and performance requirements for the Project. It establishes the outcomes that the Contractor is required to achieve and forms the basis upon which the Contractor will develop, coordinate, design, construct, commission and hand over the Works.

The Works will be delivered under an AS 4300–1995 Design and Construct Contract, under which the Contractor will assume full responsibility for the detailed design, design coordination, statutory approvals, construction, commissioning, testing and handover of the completed facility, except where expressly stated otherwise in the Contract.

This Project is funded under the Australian Government Growing Regions Program. In accordance with the Project Funding Agreement, the Head Contractor must hold and maintain current accreditation under the Australian Government Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme (the Scheme) for the entirety of the Contract.

Tenderers must:

a)	hold current accreditation under the Australian Government Work Health and Safety Accreditation Scheme at the Tender Closing Time;

b)	provide evidence of current accreditation with their Tender submission;

c)	maintain accreditation for the duration of the Contract, including any extensions of time or defects liability period where accreditation is required to remain in force; and

d)	immediately notify the Principal of any actual or proposed suspension, lapse, cancellation or variation to their accreditation status.

A non-mandatory Tender Site Briefing will be held on Monday, 5 October 2026, 1.30 pm (AEST). The location of the meeting will commence at Proserpine Administration Building, 83-85 Main Street, Proserpine Qld 4800 and will progress to the Site Visit at Shute Harbour Road and Brandy Creek Road. Access to the Site is adjacent to the bus stop pair refer to the Conditions of Tender clause 7 for a map for parking at the Site.

N.B. PPE is a requirement to attend this site, at a minimum Hi-Vis long-sleeved shirt, full length pants, steel cap boots and eye protection, it is also recommended to wear sun protection.

Please confirm your attendance at this meeting via contracts@whitsundayrc.qld.gov.au no later than midday, Thursday, 1 October 2026.

All communications must go through the VendorPanel communications forum.

publicQuestions.question: Is a company able to price part B horticulture only?
publicQuestions.answer: Yes, companies are permitted to price one part only.

publicQuestions.question:
Hello,

In the Tender pricing excel spreadsheet, are we able to reorder the sites by suburb?

The sites are in a random order and re-organizing them would allow for easier scoping and data input.

Thanks
publicQuestions.answer:
Sites can be reorganised by suburb.

However please note, tenderers should exercise care when reviewing and updating pricing in Table 1 – Summary Part A, as different Site Types have different service frequencies.

For example, Rural sites are serviced quarterly, and the associated formula is based on four (4) services per annum.

Tenderers are responsible for ensuring that any formulas remain accurate following any reorganisation of the spreadsheet.

publicQuestions.question: Can we choose between horticulture or mowing? And should I bid for all parks and reserves or can select specific one's ?
publicQuestions.answer:
Can we choose between horticulture or mowing?

Yes. Tenderers may submit for Part A, Part B, or both Parts A and B. However, Council's current intention is not to award both parts to the same contractor.

Do we need to bid for all parks and reserves, or can we select specific sites?

No. Tenderers must submit pricing for all sites within the relevant tender part. Partial submissions for selected parks, reserves or sites will not be considered compliant. For example, a tender submission for Part A must include pricing for all Part A sites.

publicQuestions.question: About 25 sites in Table 1 (rows 181 to 205) say Monthly but the formula multiplies by 4. Is it 4 or 12 visits a year?
publicQuestions.answer:
The formula in Column P of Table 1 – Part A – Lump Sum should be multiplied by 12 visits for Rows 182 to 205.

Tenderers should allow for 12 Routine Maintenance Interventions (RMIs) per annum for these items when completing their pricing.

The tender pricing sheet has been updated and added as Addendum1:

2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - UPDATED Section B - Attachment 1 - Schedule 2 - Tender Prices - Addendum 1

publicQuestions.question:
Good Morning,

We refer to document titled “2627-17 – Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services – Section D – Attachment 2 – Part A & B – Assets Table”.

We have identified the following discrepancies in the Road Reserves tab:

Q1. Row 86 appears to duplicate the information provided in Row 80. Can Council confirm if this is correct?

Q2. The street address for Row 89 appears to be missing. Can Council provide the applicable street address?

Can Council please clarify these matters and, if necessary, issue an amended spreadsheet?

Kind Regards
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1. Council confirms that Row 86 is a duplicate of Row 80 and was included in error. Duplicate has now been removed.

Q2. Council confirms the street address for Brady Road Overpass is - Next to 83 Brady Road, Dandenong North.

An amended Assets Table has been re-issued reflecting the above corrections.

2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - Section D - Attachment 2 - Part A & B - Assets Table - Addendum 2

publicQuestions.question: When reviewing the asset list included with the attachments, is there any indication as which sites will require traffic management? Are sites listed as road reserves the only sites that will require traffic management?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council advises that Assets Table (Section D – Attachment 2) does not identify sites requiring traffic management.

Traffic management may be required at locations other than road reserves, depending on site-specific conditions and operational requirements.

Tenderers are encouraged to utilise the geopackage and associated asset location information to assess likely traffic management requirements.

Tenderers should make their own assessment and allow for any necessary traffic management within their submission.

publicQuestions.question:
Pricing Schedule – Site-Specific Pricing Clarification

The pricing schedule requests a rate per square metre (m²) for each site.

Could you please confirm whether contractors are permitted to provide an individually calculated fixed price for each site, rather than applying a standard m² rate?

The level of maintenance required varies significantly between sites due to factors such as trimming requirements, site layout, accessibility and walking distances.

Applying a standard m² rate across all sites may not accurately reflect the actual labour and maintenance requirements of each location.

We believe that pricing each site individually would allow for a more accurate and competitive quotation that better reflects the work required.
publicQuestions.answer:
Council acknowledges that maintenance requirements vary between sites.

Tenderers can submit pricing on a site-by-site basis, or apply a uniform rate to all sites, provided pricing is provided per intervention (Column O) and annual cost (Column P).

publicQuestions.question: In Relation to the SOR items for Mulch (S2.1,2 & 3), can I confirm if there is plant & Equipment available for Loading at Council Stockpile location or should the Contractor allow for Floating of equipment for loading in m3 rate? To avoid inflated rates, would an additional rate item be preferred for Floats / Plant etc ?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council advises that no Council plant or equipment will be available for loading mulch at stockpile locations.

Tenderers should allow for all labour, plant, equipment, transport and associated costs required to load, collect and deliver mulch within the nominated Schedule of Rates items.

No additional rate item is proposed.

publicQuestions.question: Can you advise what application is required to view the contents of the .GPGK files provided ?
publicQuestions.answer:
Council advises that files provided in GeoPackage (.GPKG) format can be viewed using GIS applications such as QGIS (free software) or ArcGIS.

Tenderers are responsible for obtaining suitable software to access and review the data.

publicQuestions.question:
The contract conditions refer to performance security equivalent to 5% of the contract sum.

Could Council confirm whether this security is mandatory for the successful contractor and what form of security is required?
publicQuestions.answer:
Yes. Performance Security is required from the successful Contractor.

The security must be equivalent to 5% of the Contract Sum and may be provided as a cheque, irrevocable bank guarantee, or insurance bond in a form approved by Council.

publicQuestions.question:
Q1 - A Granitic	Please confirm how the 43 granitic path/hardstand asset areas in Part A Attachment 2, totalling 32,262.14 m², are to be priced, given that no separate corresponding rows appear in Part A Table 1 of Schedule 2. Are these areas intended to be included within existing lump sum mowing items, or will a revised pricing schedule be issued to separately identify these assets?

Q2 - B Areas	Please confirm the quantities to be used for Crompton, Darby and Marconi Drive (2,865.04m² versus 6,008.99m²) and Thornton Court (9-13) Reserve (1,145.13m² versus 9,042.27m²), as the Part B tender prices and Addendum 2 assets differ.

Q3 - Batter	Please confirm whether Springvalley Reserve Batter is to receive 4 RMIs p.a. as specified in the Part A pricing schedule or 12 RMIs p.a. as shown in the Addendum 2 asset schedule.

Q4 - Allocated Admin It	Please confirm whether the dedicated contract and operational administration and technology/systems administrator positions may be allocated fractional FTE subject to a named, dedicated point of accountability and full delivery of Council's required reporting and system obligations.

Q5 - Outcome Frequency	Please confirm how additional maintenance attendance required to achieve specified Service Outcomes under clause 6.8.3 will be distinguished from Council-directed changes to Service Frequencies treated as variations under clause 6.8.4, particularly where the prescribed 12 or 4 RMIs per annum are insufficient to maintain the required standards.
publicQuestions.answer:
1.	Council confirms that the granitic path and hardstand asset areas identified in Part A Attachment 2, form part of the service scope.

Please see updated Tender Prices Table.

Note: Table 1 – Part A Lump Sum Tab now includes Granitic path and Hardstands Assets. To receive four (4) \interventions per annum as per the specification.

2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - UPDATED Section B - Attachment 1 - Schedule 2 - Tender Prices - ADDENDUM 3

Please see updated Assets Table. Note Part A – Granitic Areas Tab has now been updated to the correct frequency of four (4) interventions per annum.

2627-17 - Mowing and Horticulture Maintenance Services - UPDATED Section D - Attachment 2 - Part A & B - Assets Table - ADDENDUM 4

2.	Council confirms the following corrections apply:

-	Crompton, Darby and Marconi Drive: the correct area is 6,008.99 m².

-	Thornton Court Reserve (9-13): the correct area is 1,142.12 m².

The Tender Price Table and Assets Table have been reviewed and updated with the correct data.

3.	Council confirms that 4 RMIs per annum is the service level required for the Springvalley Reserve Batter.

4.	Tenderers are to provide an overall organisational chart and chart depicting personnel responsible for the delivery of the services.

Tenderers are to provide a list of all in house staff that will be allocated to the carry out the works for this Contract.

This list should include all Key Personnel intended to be engaged in the management and delivery of the works as per the specification including percentage of time key personnel are solely dedicated to service this contract.

5.	6.8.3 Service Frequencies – Contractors are required to achieve applicable service outcomes during interventions.

When service outcomes are not met, the Contractor may be issued with a corrective action from Council, directing them to make a return visit and ensure service outcomes are met.

Changes to specified frequency will be issued as a variation in accordance with 6.8.4 of the Specification.

This is in an instance where Council has directed additional interventions beyond the specified service program.

These additional interventions will be treated as a Variation in accordance with the Specification.

publicQuestions.question:
Conflicting information:

1. Schedule 1 Tender Form states "The tendered amounts include GST and are not subject to cost adjustment." This form will be signed by the tenderer.
