Alternative inclusion: “If the Provider assumes responsibility for Resident or invitee damage irrespective of its fault, that responsibility is subject to an agreed funded allowance and aggregate cap of [agreed amount] per [agreed period].”

“Before charging the Provider, the State must provide evidence of causation and reasonable repair costs, consult on non-emergency works and credit insurance proceeds and other recoveries. There must be no double recovery of repair costs and insurance excesses. An excess is payable only to the extent attributable to damage for which the Provider is responsible and within the agreed cap.”

Apply the agreed allocation consistently across clause 7.4, clause 13.2, special condition 7 and Annexure 1.

8. Alignment of lease obligations and funding Reference Schedule; special condition 3; Annexure 4. Variation requested: Align the lease with service funding and agree funding for maintenance, servicing, resident damage and after-hours support.

Amendment proposed: Inclusion: Complete the term to align with the service-funding agreement and attach an agreed funding and cost-allocation schedule.

“If funding is materially reduced, ceases or is insufficient to meet the agreed obligations, the parties must promptly review funding, scope and performance requirements. The Provider is not required to subsidise an unfunded shortfall from its own resources. If revised arrangements are not agreed within [agreed review period], the Provider may terminate on notice sufficient for an orderly resident transition.”

“Any obligation to seek additional public or private funding is a reasonable-endeavours obligation only, does not guarantee receipt of funding and does not require the Provider to use unrestricted funds to underwrite the service.”

9. Termination for convenience and transition costs Clause.4. Variation requested: Allow at least six months for an orderly transition and reimburse unavoidable transition and approved unrecouped establishment costs.

Amendment proposed: Replace the notice and compensation provisions in clause 12.4(a):

“The State may terminate for convenience on not less than six months’ written notice, or such longer period as the parties reasonably agree is required for safe resident transition. Where termination is not caused by the Provider’s default, the State must reimburse reasonable and unavoidable transition costs and approved establishment expenditure not yet recouped, after deducting amounts already funded or otherwise recovered.”

Inclusion: Require an agreed transition plan covering continued accommodation, transfer of Resident agreements, information and monies, allocation of costs and reasonable cooperation. Align the transfer deadlines with that plan.

10. Material default, cure periods and proportionate step-in Clauses 12.1-12.3; clause 7.5. Variation requested: Restrict termination to material breaches and give Mission Australia a reasonable opportunity to remedy before termination or step-in.

Amendment proposed: “For a breach capable of remedy, the State must give written particulars and allow at least 20 Business Days to remedy before termination. If remedy reasonably requires longer, the Provider must commence within that period and diligently complete it within a reasonable agreed period. Cross-default applies only to a material breach of an agreement directly relevant to delivery of the Program at the Premises.”

“Immediate step-in is permitted only to the extent reasonably necessary to address an urgent safety risk or serious service-continuity risk. Otherwise, step-in requires prior notice and expiry of a reasonable remedy period. Recoverable costs must be reasonable, itemised and directly attributable to remedying the Provider’s default.”

Align clause 7.5 repair notices with reasonable completion timeframes, taking account of urgency, contractor availability and the nature of the work.

11. Changes to specifications and operational requirements. Clause 5.2; special conditions 5-6; Annexure 4. Variation requested: Specify the requirements applying to this CAP site and agree funding and implementation arrangements before material cost increases take effect.

Amendment proposed: Inclusion: Attach a site-specific schedule of applicable CAP outputs, performance measures, staffing, cleaning and after-hours support requirements.

“A change to Program Specifications or operational requirements that materially increases the Provider’s cost, staffing or scope takes effect only after consultation and written agreement on additional funding, revised obligations and reasonable implementation time. Fault-response measures distinguish initial response and make-safe action from final rectification. The Provider is not responsible for completing State-allocated work or for delays attributable to the State.”

12. Defined outgoings and disputed charges. Clause 1.1; clauses 3-4. Variation requsted: Limit recoverable charges to agreed items and permit genuine invoice disputes.

The State should pay false-alarm costs caused by defective State equipment.

Amendment proposed: “Outgoings means only the charges expressly listed in the agreed Outgoings Schedule. It excludes capital expenditure, defect rectification, State-responsibility work and costs attributable to the State’s breach, negligence or wrongful conduct. Existing exclusions, including local authority rates and land tax, are retained.”

“A demand for reimbursement must include supporting invoices and sufficient particulars. The Provider may withhold a genuinely disputed amount pending resolution, must promptly give reasons for the dispute and must pay undisputed amounts when due. Withholding a disputed amount under this provision is not a default.”

“The State is responsible for unwanted fire-alarm attendance charges caused by defective State equipment, original installation defects or failure to perform State-allocated maintenance.”

13. Make-good limited to Provider responsibilities. Clause 16; special condition 11. Variation requested: Use the commencement condition report as the benchmark and exclude wear and tear, defects and State-responsibility work.

Amendment proposed: “The Provider must return the Premises by reference to the agreed commencement condition report, excluding fair wear and tear, original or latent defects, end-of-life deterioration and work allocated to the State. Reinstatement of approved alterations is required only where expressly agreed when consent is given. The Provider remains responsible for damage caused by removal of its Property.”

“The State must provide particulars and reasonable, evidenced costs for any proposed make-good charge and allow the Provider a reasonable opportunity to inspect, remedy or dispute the claim. The State may not recover more than the reasonable cost of work for which the Provider is responsible.”

Retain the existing fair-wear-and-tear protection for Non-Residential Space and apply equivalent protection to the whole Premises.

publicQuestions.question: Can the Dept confirm that the costs which are to be absorbed by the Provider under the lease (eg repair and maintenance, outgoings, connection of all services, maintenance for non-standard equipment, planned maintenance, responsive maintenance etc) will form part of the funding to be provided by the Department under the Service Agreement? Or is it the case that the Provider is required to fund these costs itself?
publicQuestions.answer:
Dear Supplier

Please see response to your question as per below:

Q. Can the Dept confirm that the costs which are to be absorbed by the Provider under the lease (eg repair and maintenance, outgoings, connection of all services, maintenance for non-standard equipment, planned maintenance, responsive maintenance etc) will form part of the funding to be provided by the Department under the Service Agreement? Or is it the case that the Provider is required to fund these costs itself?

A. The Provider is responsible for meeting the property-related obligations outlined in the lease, this includes planned maintenance and responsive maintenance, connection of services etc.

Providers should take these obligations into consideration when assessing the operational and financial requirements of delivering the service. The Department's funding contribution is provided to support the delivery of the contracted service and is not intended to operate as a separate reimbursement arrangement for individual property-related costs. The Provider is responsible for managing these expenses within its available funding and operational arrangements.

Providers may be approved for an exemption from certain maintenance obligations under the Crisis Accommodation Program (CAP) lease agreement for department-owned CAP properties. This is referred to as a maintenance exemption. Maintenance exemptions are assessed and approved on the grounds of financial hardship.

Kind Regards

Procurement Team

Question: The lease agreement is a three-year agreement. If the service is to start on 1 Feb 2027, the three-year lease will run across four financial years. The budget templates in the Expenditure Plan provides templates for three years. Should the budget Year 1 start with service delivery on 1 Feb 2027 or 1 July 2027?

Answer: The Expenditure Plan is intended to demonstrate the annual funding amounts over the term of the agreement. Respondents should prepare the budget based on the anticipated service commencement date. As lease commencement is dependent on construction completion, the final funding amounts will be apportioned on a monthly basis and adjusted across the applicable financial years once the commencement date is confirmed.

Question: The Funding Schedule states that children/young people aged 13-18 are to be accommodated. Will the supplier be required to provide case management? Are children to be included in the KPIs?

Answer: The Funding Schedule specifies that the service is intended for eligible clients who are single adults or adult couples experiencing, or at risk of, homelessness. As such, respondents are not required to provide case management services for children or young people aged 13–18 years, and children are not included within the service KPIs. Clause 8.7, Services Targeting Young People, is noted in the documentation as, “Clause Not in Use’ and as such is not applicable to this procurement and should be disregarded.

title: Support the design, development, testing, validation of the FarmTechConnect AgTech Adoption program
description:
The Department of Primary Industries (DPI) is seeking supplier/s to provide specialist professional services supporting DPI-led delivery of FarmTechConnect. The supplier may engage subcontractors with relevant specialist expertise and will remain responsible for coordinating and delivering all contracted services and outputs. DPI will retain overall responsibility for program leadership, producer-facing delivery and relationships with project partners.

DPI requires a consistent approach that enables extension providers to support producers to identify priority farm business challenges, assess digital readiness, evaluate suitable technologies and return on investment, develop staged adoption plans, and implement and integrate technology into existing production systems. The program must support productivity, profitability and resilience outcomes, with a primary focus on red meat enterprises and application to relevant mixed-farming systems.

The supplier will translate the pilot’s findings, experience and available resources into an integrated package comprising the program framework, producer workbook, extension workflows, digital literacy learning materials, decision-support resources, facilitator training and implementation guidance. Existing pilot outputs must be assessed and retained, refined or adapted where appropriate, with additional development directed towards identified gaps.

The project aims to preserve and protect the heritage building & the health service it houses by replacing the deteriorated roofing materials with new, heritage approved, products. vendorPanelDetails.background:
This heritage listed place, Unara, is a heritage-listed detached Federation Bungalow, originally built for Sir Littleton Groom Circa 1906. The Northern and Southern wings were added in the 1950’s & 1960’s respectively. Along with various alterations & additions over the years. The building currently houses Drug & Alcohol residential rehabilitation.

The building is currently experiencing roof leaks, with some isolated interior damage caused. It has been determined that new roofing including flashings and stormwater reticulation remediation is required. Structural tie down and insulation will be improved while the sheeting is off and the chimneys will be repointed to retain their integrity.

The stormwater reticulation downstream of the downpipes is in a failed state. The above ground reticulation, suspended from the floor joists, appears to have backfalls and some charged lines. Reticulation enters the ground on the Western side of the Northern extension, via a retention pipe which is currently disconnected from the inground pipe, discharging all stormwater to surface in the undercroft. This is presumably because the inground system is blocked. The inground stormwater reticulation direction, route & discharge point is unknown.

RFI01 - EOT Request

Hi Julianne,

We respectfully request an Extension of Time (EOT) for the submission of our tender for the Sludge Dewatering Upgrade Project, extending the current submission deadline of 5 November 2026 to 20 November 2026.

This extension is requested to allow sufficient time to obtain and assess vendor package pricing, receive outstanding subcontractor quotations, and develop a complete and accurate tender submission that adequately addresses the complexities and various elements of the project.

The current tender timeframe has presented several challenges, including:

•	Vendor package pricing and lead times: The specialised nature of the sludge dewatering equipment requires engagement with multiple vendors to obtain compliant technical and commercial offers. Allowing sufficient time for vendors to review the project requirements and develop their submissions is essential.

•	Subcontractor responses: A number of subcontractor quotations remain outstanding, with additional time required to obtain, review and clarify pricing to ensure all relevant scope elements are adequately covered.

•	Limited supplier participation: Several suppliers have declined to provide pricing due to the short turnaround time available. This has restricted the number of competitive quotations received and increased the time required to identify and engage alternative suppliers.

•	Project complexity and scope coordination: The project involves multiple interfacing elements, vendor packages and subcontracted works that require careful coordination to ensure the proposed solution is technically compliant and commercially complete.

•	Tender accuracy and completeness: Additional time is required to review vendor and subcontractor submissions, reconcile scope gaps and exclusions, confirm pricing assumptions, and undertake a detailed internal review of the estimate and overall tender submission.

The requested extension will provide the necessary opportunity to obtain more complete and reliable pricing, properly assess the associated risks and exclusions, and ensure our final submission represents an accurate and considered offer that meets the project requirements.

We believe the additional time will support a more robust and competitive tender submission, reducing the likelihood of pricing omissions, scope gaps or assumptions that may otherwise affect the delivery and cost certainty of the project.

We therefore respectfully request approval to extend the tender submission deadline by 15 calendar days, from 5 November 2026 to 20 November 2026.

Thank you for your consideration of this request. We look forward to your response.

Kind regards,

title: Identity Governance Administration (IGA) & Privileged Access Management (PAM) Solutions and Services
description:
Suppliers are invited by the State of Queensland (acting through the Department of Transport and Main Roads (TMR) – the Customer) to submit Offers for either one or both Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) Solution and / or Privileged Access Management (PAM) Solution and associated maintenance and support Services as further specified in this Invitation to Offer (ITO) TMRICT26098.

Suppliers may submit an Offer for:

	(a) an IGA Solution, maintenance and support Services only; or

	(b) a PAM Solution, maintenance and support Services only; or

	(c) both an IGA Solution and PAM Solution, with maintenance and support Services for both/each; or

	(d) a single Solution that meets the Requirements for both IGA and PAM, with maintenance and support Services.

All technology types will be considered (that is, Suppliers are not limited to submitting Offers for As a Service based solutions only), as well as alternative and innovative solutions which meet the Customer’s objectives and Requirements.

The Requirements are set out in the Invitation Documents and include the following in-scope Products and Services:

(a) IGA Solution and Services: a solution to satisfy the identity governance and administration Requirements including:

 (i) all applicable product components such as Licensed Software including modules, connectors, agents and related third party software (if any); and/or

 (ii) all applicable hosted components such as Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) / Platform as a Service (PaaS) including modules, connectors and agents (if any); and

 (iii) associated ongoing maintenance and support Services such as monitoring, maintenance, provision of updates, patches, new releases, remedial response and rectification, and provision of user documentation and continuous improvement; and/or

(b) PAM Solution and Services: a solution to satisfy the privileged access management Requirements, including:

 (i) all applicable product components such as Licensed Software including modules, connectors, agents and related third party software; and Hardware or on-premise installed components (if any); and/or

 (ii) all applicable hosted components such as Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) / Platform as a Service (PaaS) including modules, connectors and agents (if any); and

 (iii) associated ongoing maintenance and support Services such as monitoring, maintenance, provision of updates, patches, new releases, remedial response and rectification, and provision of user documentation and continuous improvement.

The following is out of scope:

	(a) configuration and customisation of the offered Solutions;

	(b) provision of integration services (other than supply of out-of-the-box connectors);

	(c) implementation services (including transition-in and transition-out services); and

	(d) end user help desk support (Level 1 Support Services) for the Customer’s end users – this will be managed by the Customer.

Any contract formed subsequent to this Invitation must be governed by the QITC Framework, Comprehensive Contract Conditions - ICT Products and Services, and the Draft Contract issued with the Invitation Documents.

Please submit all enquiries or clarifications directly through Vendor Panel.

publicQuestions.question:
Please can TMR provide the following clarifications ASAP:

1.	Support levels conflict. Schedule TMR1 s11.5 makes Level 2 the Customer’s and Level 3 the Supplier’s after hypercare. Module Order Forms 2B and 3 make Level 2 the Supplier’s, add Level 4 vendor escalation, and MOF 3 includes support for integration configuration and maintenance. Which applies?

2.	Australia-only. MR2 bars access to Customer Data from outside Australia, and MOF 2B requires support personnel in Australia, yet it also requires Level 4 escalation to the software publisher. Does vendor engineering escalation without Customer Data access comply?

3.	Certification minimums differ. Response Schedules B and C list ISO 27001:2022, SOC 2 Type II, 27017 and 27018 as minimum. TMR1 s15 requires at least two standards. Contract item 34 requires ISO 27001:2022 plus two more. Which is correct?

4.	Pricing workbook errors. IGA Total Offered Price: the Year 4 licensed-software cell repeats Year 3 (links to L103, should be N103). PAM Total Offered Price, licensed-software row, Years 2 to 5 link to the wrong columns (G8 to J113, H8 and I8 to L113, J8 to P113). Table 1.3 rows 96 to 101 have offset references, and the hidden Scenarios tab has a #REF! error. The cells are locked. How should suppliers correct them? The as-a-service rows appear correct. Please issue a corrected workbook.

5.	Environments. The pricing tables drop the test environment after the build, but TMR1 s10 requires separate prod, dev and UAT. How many non-production environments should we price?

6.	Acceptance and payment. 80% of the IGA licence price falls due at connector and SAP/RACF integration milestones that depend on CyberCX work, with a zero-defect test. What deems acceptance if the delay is TMR’s or CyberCX’s?

7.	Subscription term. MOF 3 has 12-month subscription periods with 60-day non-renewal notice, and also a 5-year minimum. Termination for convenience carries no extra amount. Which governs?

8.	Schedule 2 deliverables 1 to 6 (blueprints, control lists, integration specifications, due 5 business days after start) look like consulting work, but implementation and integration are out of scope. Who writes them, and are they priced?

9.	Departures. MR1 says the Conditions and Modules are non-negotiable, but Schedule A s11 invites departures to the Draft QITC Contract. Which parts can we depart from?

10.	Fix Time ends only when TMR confirms in writing. Can there be deemed confirmation after a set period?

11.	Availability SLA and service credits: confirm they apply only to as-a-service components, not licensed software.

12.	Test environment readiness (Schedule 9) shows the responsible party as blank. Who provides it?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to the Addendum List issued 4 November 2026 which includes responses to these questions.

title: RFT(EXC00136) Flood and River Level Monitoring Services for Townsville City Council
description:
Townsville City Council requires a vendor led solution under Stream B of the Enviromon Replacement project. The solution must replace the operational capability currently provided by Enviromon and TARDIS for the receipt, processing, storage, visualisation, alerting, reporting and onward distribution of flood warning observation data.

Council currently relies on ALERT rainfall and water level gauge data to support disaster management, flood modelling, situational awareness and operational decision making across the Townsville Local Government Area. The Bureau of Meteorology has advised that support for Enviromon will cease in October 2026, and TARDIS is expected to reach end of support in 2027. The replacement solution must therefore provide a sustainable, secure and future ready capability that supports continuity of Council’s flood warning data operations before legacy support risks become unacceptable.

The Supplier must provide a commercially available, configurable cloud SaaS solution and associated implementation services. The Supplier must not propose a tactical in house build as the primary solution. The intent of this Scope is to obtain a mature, supportable and secure platform that can be implemented, tested, transitioned into operation and supported under agreed service levels.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi, could you please provide guidance for the following questions?

1. Export formats (US03, US41, FR47, FR74, NFR 6.2.1): US03 requests export in .hydsys format, while US41 and NFR 6.2.1 require export in non-proprietary formats. Hydsys is a proprietary Kisters format. Is Hydsys export required, or are open formats such as CSV and JSON acceptable? If Hydsys is required, can Council provide the format specification or a sample file?

2. Thresholds by gauge type (US52): US52 is listed as "Won't Have", but its rationale states the capability must be preserved as a minimum. Is US52 required, given US53 requires thresholds to be set for each gauge?

3. Deleting data (US12, US34, FR21): Some requirements refer to deleting data and sites, while others require data to be retained for traceability. Can Council confirm that authorised users may delete data, provided every deletion is logged?

4. IFD source (US05, US06, FR77): Are Bureau of Meteorology design rainfall IFD curves acceptable, or does Council expect IFD analysis derived from its own gauge records?

5. Additional observation sources (US17): Which external observation sources does Council intend to include (for example, wind, temperature and tide data), and who provides them?

6. Output format specifications (FR47, FR70): Can Council provide specifications for the HHRR and EM-RRD_FEDSS (Waterride) formats?

7. Data classification (NFR 1.3.14, 1.3.18, 2.7.8): NFR 2.7.8 states the data is classified PROTECTED, while flood gauge data appears to be OFFICIAL. Can Council confirm the classification?

Thank you,
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry. Please find response below marked with **

1. Export formats (US03, US41, FR47, FR74, NFR 6.2.1): US03 requests export in .hydsys format, while US41 and NFR 6.2.1 require export in non-proprietary formats. Hydsys is a proprietary Kisters format. Is Hydsys export required, or are open formats such as CSV and JSON acceptable? If Hydsys is required, can Council provide the format specification or a sample file?

** CSV export is acceptable and preferred. Export in .hydsys format is not required. Suppliers should provide export functionality in open, non proprietary formats, such as CSV, to support data portability and interoperability.

2. Thresholds by gauge type (US52): US52 is listed as "Won't Have", but its rationale states the capability must be preserved as a minimum. Is US52 required, given US53 requires thresholds to be set for each gauge?

** Council confirms US52 should be changed from "Won't Have" to "Should Have". This requirement applies to operational thresholds common across all gauges, such as communication failures and low battery voltage alerts. Gauge specific thresholds remain covered under US53.

3. Deleting data (US12, US34, FR21): Some requirements refer to deleting data and sites, while others require data to be retained for traceability. Can Council confirm that authorised users may delete data, provided every deletion is logged?

** Council confirms authorised administrators may update or delete data, provided all changes are logged and auditable. Historical records for critical data changes, such as survey offset values, should be retained to maintain a complete audit trail.

4. IFD source (US05, US06, FR77): Are Bureau of Meteorology design rainfall IFD curves acceptable, or does Council expect IFD analysis derived from its own gauge records?

** Council confirms Intensity Frequency Duration (IFD) data must be sourced from the Bureau of Meteorology's Design Rainfall Intensity Frequency Duration datasets. Council generated rainfall analyses derived from local gauge records are not required.

5. Additional observation sources (US17): Which external observation sources does Council intend to include (for example, wind, temperature and tide data), and who provides them?

** Council confirms additional observation data, including wind, temperature and tide data, should primarily be sourced from the Bureau of Meteorology. The solution should also support approved Council operated data sources where available, providing flexibility to use either source based on operational requirements.

6. Output format specifications (FR47, FR70): Can Council provide specifications for the HHRR and EM-RRD_FEDSS (Waterride) formats?

** Council confirms HHRR and EM-RRD_FEDSS outputs relate to Geographic Information System (GIS) grid based water level and depth data used within Council's flood modelling and decision support environment. Suppliers may propose equivalent formats capable of storing and exchanging the same information and supporting integration with Council's WaterRide and Flood Emergency Decision Support System workflows.

7. Data classification (NFR 1.3.14, 1.3.18, 2.7.8): NFR 2.7.8 states the data is classified PROTECTED, while flood gauge data appears to be OFFICIAL. Can Council confirm the classification?

** Council confirms the information managed by the solution is expected to be classified as OFFICIAL. Suppliers should respond on this basis. Council reserves the right to review and amend the classification during contract negotiations or implementation if required by information security, privacy or legal obligations.

Yours sincerely,

Townsville City Council

publicQuestions.answer:

publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your enquiry. Please find response below marked with **

1. Will a business continuity plan certified under the supplier’s ISO 27001 system and aligned to ISO 22301 be accepted for NFR 2.8.2?

** Council confirms a Business Continuity Plan certified under ISO 27001 and aligned with ISO 22301 will satisfy this requirement.

2. Can TCC provide the interface specifications for connecting to legacy Enviromon? Will these connections by UDP, TCP/IP, or other?

** Council advises suppliers should refer to the Conceptual tab within EXC00136 Flood and River Level Monitoring Services - RFT - Schedule 3 - Requirements Response Schedule v1.0.

** Council advises suppliers should refer to the requirements schedule and respond based on their proposed approach and capability to undertake any historical data migration requirements.

** Council confirms the information managed by the solution is expected to be classified as OFFICIAL. Suppliers should respond on this basis. Council reserves the right to review and amend the classification during contract negotiations or implementation if required by information security, privacy or legal obligations.

5. Can you please provide these documents that are referenced in the scope:

the BoM Enviromon Replacement Functional Requirements Guide, the Queensland Reconstruction Authority’s flood warning infrastructure guidance (FWIN SOW guidance).

** Council advises suppliers should refer to the Bureau of Meteorology website and the Queensland Reconstruction Authority website for the relevant documentation, including the Enviromon Replacement Functional Requirements Guide and Flood Warning Infrastructure Network guidance.

6. Can TCC supply interface specifications for the export formats HHRR, HYDSYS and EM-RRD_FEDSS (output for Waterride).

** Council confirms the following definitions

- Raw data: Data received directly from a sensor without processing

- Derived data: Data generated through aggregation or accumulation of raw data.

- Calculated data: Data produced using calibration factors or calculation rules. Historical rules and effective dates must be retained to support interpretation and recalculation.

title: Culvert Replacement Works - Kellys Road, Omeo Valley
description:
Two existing failing pipe culverts that are located along Kellys Road over minor tributaries of the Mitta Mitta River are the subject of this report. At each of the sites, an existing reinforced concrete pipe culvert has deteriorated in condition to the extent that the East Gippsland Shire Council is investigating repair or replacement works.

An assessment of the existing sites has been carried out to determine and assess the range of options available for replacing each of the culverts. It is proposed for Site A that the existing DN1200 mm concrete pipe be replaced with single cell reinforced concrete culvert on a similar horizontal and vertical alignment as currently exists. The existing DN900 mm pipe at Site B can be repaired to a serviceable condition by re-laying the pipes at the culvert outlet.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Kellys Road extends from the south east end of the Omeo Valley Road, which follows the Livingstone Creek from the Omeo Highway to the Hinnomunjie bridge across the Mitta Mitta River. The section of Kellys Road that is under the control of the East Gippsland Shire Council continues for 9.7 km to the Nine Mile Creek crossing. The road section that is the subject of this report was reconstructed and substantially upgraded by the former Omeo Shire Council in the early 1970’s, in accordance with an overall strategy to establish an alternative route between Omeo and Mitta Mitta that was less susceptible to winter snowfalls.

The road initially passes through open farmland that is used for stock grazing, before entering the Alpine National Park. The road section has a formed and gravelled surface, which is well maintained by the Council. The road has been subjected to oversize vehicles for past logging and bushfire suppression operations in the area but is predominately used for access to the farm properties, as well as by 4WD based visitors to numerous camping spots along the nearby Mitta Mitta River and within the National Park.

publicQuestions.question: Can you please clarify if the costs for geomembrane destructive testing and independent testing of geosynthetic material is to be included in this tender? publicQuestions.answer:
Council confirms that tenderers are to include costs for geomembrane destructive testing and independent geosynthetic material testing as part of their tender submission.

Geomembrane destructive testing is already included under Item 16 of the Schedule of Rates and should be priced per test. As outlined in Clause 7.3.8.5 of S14, Council is responsible for the initial laboratory testing costs, with any additional testing resulting from failed destructive tests being the responsibility of the Geosynthetic Contractor.

Independent conformance testing of the GCL, HDPE geomembrane and protection and separation geotextiles is also required under the CQA Specification and S14. Tenderers should include separate rates for these tests under the ""Please insert any other applicable rates required to complete the works in accordance with the Specification"" section of the Schedule of Rates, including any associated sampling, transport and laboratory reporting costs.

Council has no objection to tenderers using their own in-house NATA-accredited laboratories, provided they are accredited for the relevant test methods, meet the independence requirements of the CQA Specification and are approved in accordance with the tender requirements.

All testing is to be carried out in accordance with the specified methods and frequencies. The Geosynthetic Contractor's existing CQC testing responsibilities remain unchanged.

publicQuestions.question:
Could Council please clarify the following so we can complete Part 3 – Schedule of Rates consistently with the intended evaluation method?

1. Quantity column

 The personnel items are measured “per Hour”, but the Quantity column is blank. Should tenderers leave this column blank, enter one hour against each role, or use another prescribed quantity? Please confirm that tenderers are not expected to nominate project-specific weekly staffing hours or minimum engagements in this column.

2. “Other” roles and total formula

 The total in G32 currently sums G20:G29 and excludes the “Other” amount in G30. Please confirm whether this is intentional or whether an amended workbook will be issued. Where additional roles such as estimator, scheduler or surveyor are offered, how should the additional lines be included in the evaluation total?

3. Category 1 pricing assessment

 The Cost/Value for Money section of the Response Forms describes rate benchmarking for each category, while the briefing’s value-for-money example refers to Category 2. Please confirm how the personnel rates will be assessed for Category 1 and combined with the qualitative evaluation.

4. GST basis

 The Schedule of Rates does not identify a GST basis. Our understanding of clause 8.8 is that rates should be GST-inclusive unless expressly stated otherwise. Please confirm the preferred basis for the workbook to ensure like-for-like comparison.
publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon please see below responses:

1. This column can be left blank. Tenderers are not expected to insert an assumed number of hours, however for comparative purposes, any quantities entered will be normalised to a figure of 1.

2. Council notes the formula does not currently include the ‘Other’ amount in G30. An updated version of the schedule of rates will be provided, which includes the nominal quantity, and exclusion of GST. Where the proponent is seeking to include additional roles, please insert a new row and complete aligning with the template.

3. Value for money will be evaluated for both Category One and Category 2, using the same formula indicated in the Response Schedules. The indicative benchmarked price score will be calculated and considered against the total weighted score achieved for each category submitted. Should the Tenderer submit alternate rates for Category 1 and Category 2, they will be benchmarked respectively and which will inform the value for money score.

4. Refer to Part 3 - Schedule or Rates Version 2 nominating rates exclusive of GST.

publicQuestions.question: Is Council open to a remotely delivered engagement, with support and training provided by video, and work carried out directly in Council’s ArcGIS Online organisation? Are there any Council IT or data policies restricting contractor access from outside Australia?
publicQuestions.answer:
Hello Ricki,

You are welcome to submit a tender, and it will be evaluated on its merits. There are no policies restricting contractor access outside Australia.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Is Council’s current environment ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Enterprise, or both? Which ArcGIS licences does Council hold (user types and quantities), and when do they renew?

2. Which datasets are already loaded into ArcGIS? What format are the remaining IntraMaps-era datasets in (for example MapInfo TAB, SQL Server, shapefile or CAD)?

3. Which property and rating system does Council use? Can it produce a scheduled export (for example CSV or a database view) of assessment number, owner names and property address?

4. Is the $30,000 Phase 1 limit exclusive of GST? Does it exclude ArcGIS software licensing and travel costs?

5. Can Phase 1 be priced as a fixed lump sum alongside the pricing schedule, with the schedule covering ongoing support after Phase 1?

6. What is Council’s expected commencement date following the 20 November decision?

7. Is remote delivery with scheduled on-site visits (for example kickoff and training) acceptable, or does Council have a minimum on-site requirement?

8. For planning proposals, will Council’s planning staff or an external planning consultant prepare the final maps to NSW planning mapping standards, with the GIS supplying the data and map templates?

9. Roughly how many staff will use the GIS (viewers, editors and field users)? Is there a nominated staff member who will own the GIS and receive mentoring?

10. Does Council use Microsoft 365 / Entra ID for staff sign-in?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council has a 3-year enterprise agreement with Esri that gives access to both ArcGIS Online and ArcGIS Enterprise. However, to my knowledge, the Enterprise was never deployed.

For User types, Enterprise should have according to the agreement:

Contributor - 5

Mobile Worker - 25

Creator - 25

Professional - 5

Professional Plus - 5

For ArcGIS Online:

Contributor - 15

Creator - 100

Mobile Worker - 100

Professional - 20

Professional Plus - 20

Viewer – 700

2. The data has been fully migrated over from IntraMaps to ArcGIS Online as feature layers and webmaps.

3. Council uses Civica Authority as its property and rating system and it is capable of exporting the data as a CSV.

4. $30,000 is exclusive of GST. Council has already procured ArcGIS software licences and the $30,000 limit is not required for this purpose. The $30,000 should include the travel cost.

5. It would be acceptable but may impact scoring in the circumstance that multiple vendors have similar offers.

6. We would be looking to engage as soon as possible after decision period.

7. Council does not have a minimum on-site requirement however would prefer on-site visits for kick-off meeting and staff training.

8. We would be looking for assistance for preparation of maps.

9. Approximately 4 staff members will consistently use the GIS initially through ‘Creator’ & ‘Professional’ user types. However, this anticipated to increase as capabilities are developed. An estimated 40 staff will use the ‘Viewer’ user type.

There is a nominated staff member for mentoring.

10. Council is currently transitioning to Microsoft 365 for staff sign in.

publicQuestions.question:
Dear Walcha Council,

Could you please respond to our two clarifications below:

1) Regarding the NDA srequiring signing - our legal team has reviwed and requests is a way to revise section 8 so this NDA does not survive indefinitely? Woolpert would prefer to put some time period, our default is 3 years, but we would agree to 5 years.

2) In relation to the multi-phase GIS roadmap strategy development - is this tender for the strategy only, or includes the deployment of the first phase GIS system?

Kind regards, Team Woolpert Australia
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council is agreeable to revising section 8 to a term of three years.

2. The tendor is meant for both the roadmap development strategy & a deployment for the first phase as outlined in the RFQ.

publicQuestions.question:
My priority questions would be:

1. ArcGIS environment: Is Council currently using ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS Enterprise, ArcGIS Pro, or a combination? What licences and subscriptions are available?

2. Existing work: What components of the transition from IntraMaps have already been completed, and what remains usable?

3. Data availability: What formats and sources contain Council's property, cadastre, water, sewer and planning datasets?

4. Property information: How is ownership data currently accessed, and what restrictions apply to its display?

5. System integration: Are there existing property, rating, asset management or document management systems that the GIS must integrate with?

6. Operational users: How many internal users will need GIS access, and is public-facing access required?

7. Budget: Is the $30,000 Phase 1 ceiling inclusive or exclusive of GST, and does it include software licences and hosting?

8. Contract arrangements: What ongoing support term and service availability does Council envisage?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council is currently using ArcGIS Online & ArcGIS Pro. Council does have access to ArcGIS Enterprise but it has not been deployed. Council has licences for:

ArcGIS Online

Professional Plus: 20

Professional: 20

Creator: 100

Contributor: 15

Mobile Worker: 100

Viewer: 700

ArcGIS Enterprise

Contributor - 5

Mobile Worker - 25

Creator - 25

Professional - 5

Professional Plus - 5

2. The data from IntraMaps has all been migrated to ArcGIS but the connection between our new GIS system and our organizations enterprise system, Civica Authority wasn’t re-established.

3. Council’s data is mainly stored in our enterprise management software, in physical records & as feature layers in our GIS.

4. Property ownership data is stored in Council’s Corporate Register software, Authority, where staff currently perform direct property enquiry searches. It is understood that Authority contained a suitable export feature to allow IntraMaps direct access to this database. Note that Council is expecting to transition to Authority Altitude in the short term.

5. The GIS solution should integrate with Authority, and Content Manager.

6. Currently only 4 users use it consistently with an estimated 40 more users in the future with access to ‘Viewer’ user role. Public-facing access is not required in the initial stage.

7. $30,000 is exclusive of GST. Council has already procured ArcGIS licences but if any additional licences/software would be needed. They can be itemized and included in proposal.

8. Council prefers a retainer model providing a dedicated allocation of support hours per week. These hours can be used for general GIS purposes, troubleshooting, advisory and other operational needs. It is noted that Council’s GIS needs will vary from week to week, and so an ‘actual hours’ may be beneficial.

publicQuestions.question:

- Worker's Compensation

- Motor Vehicles

The proposed CMMS must provide comprehensive facilities and asset management functionality, including asset lifecycle management, planned and reactive maintenance, work order management, contractor management, mobile workforce capability, compliance and statutory maintenance management, reporting, dashboards, and full audit trail functionality.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
The QPS has identified a strategic requirement to enhance the delivery and management of its workplace and facilities services.

QPS currently utilises the ServiceNow IT Service Management (ITSM) platform. While the ITSM platform has been adapted to support some business requirements, the extensive customisation required has not delivered the intended outcomes. This approach has resulted in operational inefficiencies, increased support and maintenance overheads, reduced system maintainability, and a user experience that does not adequately meet Facilities Management business requirements.

The required CMMS Solution will support facilities management functions across the Queensland Parliamentary Precinct and 97 Electorate Offices located throughout Queensland, including Central Queensland, Far North Queensland, North Queensland, Southeast Queensland, Southwest Queensland, and the Wide Bay Burnett region. The proposed system will enhance facilities operations by streamlining processes and improving data accuracy.

The solution must provide native FM - CMMS capability in the current released product and must be capable of implementation without substantial customisation or bespoke development.

The QPS is not seeking a generic workflow, case management, ITSM, service desk or enterprise application platform that requires the configuration or development of core FM - CMMS functions. Responses that rely on custom code, bespoke development, custom workflows, custom objects, third-party applications, or future product roadmap functionality to satisfy mandatory requirements may be assessed as non-conforming.

Shortlisted tenderers may, upon request, be required to provide a demonstration of their proposed solution to key QPS stakeholders.

Please refer to '2026LAQ035 - ITO' and ‘2026LAQ035 – Appendix 1 – Facilities Maintenance Software Requirements’ for the detailed requirements.

title: Application Control
description:
Queensland Treasury seeks to procure and implement an enterprise-grade Application Control solution that enables organisation-wide enforcement of the ASD Essential Eight Application Control strategy across all supported endpoint and server platforms, as well as align with the Information Security Manual (ISM).

The Customer has issued this Invitation to Offer with the objectives of achieving consistent application control enforcement across all endpoints and improved cyber resilience and compliance outcomes through sourcing a solution that will:

•	Support achievement and maintenance of ASD Essential Eight Maturity Level 2 and Level 3 requirements.

•	Provide application allowlisting and execution control.

•	Reduce operational overhead associated with policy administration.

•	Improve visibility, governance and reporting.

•	Support Windows, macOS, Linux and server operating environments.

•	Integrate with Treasury's broader endpoint security ecosystem.

•	Deliver high availability and enterprise scalability.

The proposed solution is required to be deployed, configured, tested and transitioned into operational support by 30 June 2027.

publicQuestions.question:
We are resubmitting the following questions as we realised we worded them incorrectly. Can Treasury please consider the following as being the actual questions posed?

//Questions:

Q.1 Could you please clarify the expected integration method for forwarding events to Queensland Treasury's Microsoft Sentinel SIEM? Specifically, should event data be ingested via API, or data connector, or is a log collector-based approach expected? (1.2.4 Auditing & Centralised Logging //pg.5)

Q.2 Can you please provide the Queensland Government information security requirements referenced? (SEC-08 //pg.12)

Q.3 Regarding 'AC-41: Solution shall allow users to request approval for blocked software with business justification', could you please clarify whether 'Solution' refers to the platform itself or to the managed service operating model? (AC-41 //pg.10)

Q.4 Regarding 'AC-41' above, If the intent is for this capability to be provided by the platform, would a process-based implementation be considered acceptable, where users submit software approval requests through a ServiceNow (or similar) workflow (including business justification) and the request is then reviewed and actioned by the managed service team? (AC-41 //pg.10)
publicQuestions.answer:
Q1 - Queensland Treasury does not mandate a single integration method. The preferred approach is to utilise a vendor-supported Microsoft Sentinel data connector where one is available. Where a supported connector is not available, API-based ingestion or another supported log-forwarding mechanism may be proposed.

Q2 - SEC-08 refers to the Queensland Government Information and Cyber Security Policy (IS18) and its mandated supporting requirements, including:

•	Queensland Government Information Security Classification Framework (QGISCF);

•	Queensland Government Data Encryption Standard;

•	Queensland Government Authentication Framework (QGAF); and

•	ASD Essential Eight strategies.

Q3 - “Solution” refers to the application control platform itself. The expectation is that, when software is blocked, the platform provides a user-facing mechanism (for example, a notification or prompt) that enables the user to initiate an approval request and provide business justification. The resulting approval workflow may integrate with the managed service operating model and/or service management tooling.

Q4 - A process-based implementation alone would not meet the intent of AC-41. The application control platform is expected to provide a user-facing mechanism, such as a notification or prompt when software is blocked, through which the user can initiate an approval request and provide business justification. The subsequent approval and fulfilment workflow may integrate with ServiceNow (or similar) and be actioned by the managed service team.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Native Windows controls (AC-18, AC-23 to AC-27) Can driver control, the Microsoft vulnerable driver blocklist and PowerShell Constrained Language Mode be delivered through Microsoft App Control for Business via Treasury’s Intune, configured by the Supplier as part of the solution?

2. Linux (BR-01, AC-01, AC-30, AC-31)

(a) Is application control required on all RHEL servers, or only internet-facing servers (per Essential Eight ML2)?

(b) Would privilege and sudo command control on RHEL, combined with RHEL’s native allowlisting (fapolicyd, RHEL 8.1+) configured by the Supplier, meet these requirements?

(c) Will RHEL 7.9 remain in scope for the contract term?

3. AC-08 AC-08 refers to “AC-63”, which doesn’t exist. Is this meant to be AC-54?

4. ServiceNow (INT-06) Which ServiceNow release and modules (e.g. ITSM, Service Catalog) does Treasury use?

5. Endpoint mix What is the split of the 3,000 endpoints and 250 servers across Windows 11, macOS, Windows Server and RHEL?

6. Current solution What application control product does Treasury use today?
publicQuestions.answer:
1 - Yes. The use of native Microsoft Windows security capabilities, including Microsoft App Control for Business deployed through Treasury’s Intune environment, may be presented as an option for meeting these requirements. Where this approach is proposed, Suppliers should consider how it aligns with BR-04 and the requirement for a unified management platform, including how the relevant controls would be managed, monitored and reported within the overall solution.

2 - (a)	Yes - Application control is required across all RHEL servers, not only internet-facing servers. The solution is intended to support Treasury’s Essential Eight ML2 requirements and progression to ML3 as per BR-07.

(b)	Suppliers may propose the use of RHEL native capabilities, including privilege/command controls and application allowlisting, as part of their solution. The approach should also be considered against BR-04, which requires a unified management platform, and AC-31, which requires consistent policy management across supported operating systems.

(c)	RHEL 7.9 is under Extended Life Cycle Support (ELS) until May 31, 2029 and may remain in scope until this date.

3 - Yes. The reference to AC-63 in AC-08 is a numbering error. The intended reference is AC-54, which requires implementation of Microsoft’s recommended application blocklist.

4 - ServiceNow Australia release with ITSM, SPM and IRM modules

5 - Windows 11 – 2667

macOS – 17

Windows Server – 191

RHEL – 65

WVD - 252

6 - Carbon Black

2. macOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux (AC-30, AC-31):

a) Do macOS and RHEL devices need to be in enforcement by 30 June 2027, or can they be delivered in a later phase within the initial term?

b) Will Treasury accept policy management and reporting unified in one platform, with enforcement on macOS and RHEL using the operating system's built-in controls or a partner product supplied under the prime supplier's contract?

c) Under Schedule C clauses 5.2 and 5.3, will offers covering some of the AC-30 platforms, or alternative offers, go through to full evaluation?

3. AC-51: Can AC-51 be met together with Treasury's existing endpoint detection and response tool, for example by matching blocked files against Microsoft Defender XDR results, or must the application control solution meet it on its own?

4. AC-21: For interpreters such as Python and Perl, will controlling which interpreter programs are allowed to run (by publisher or file hash) meet AC-21?

5. Existing application control (section 1.3.4): Please name the application control product or products in use today, whether they are in audit or enforcement mode, and roughly how many devices they cover.

6. Applications: Please provide the approximate number of applications in use across workstations and servers, and how they are deployed and updated today (for example Intune, Configuration Manager, self-updating applications, or user-installed software).

7. Rapid7: Table 10 asks for pricing for Rapid7 integration, but Rapid7 is not in the requirements. Please confirm which Rapid7 product Treasury uses and what the integration should do.

8. Hosting: Does Treasury prefer supplier-hosted SaaS or hosting in Treasury's own Azure environment, and must all data stay in Australia?
publicQuestions.answer:
1 - Answered in a previous clarification response

2 - a)	Yes, they must be in enforcement by 30 June 2027 as per the requirement for the proposed solution to be deployed, configured, tested and transitioned into operational support by 30 June 2027.

b)	Suppliers may propose the use of native capabilities for enforcement on macOS and RHEL as part of their solution. Suppliers should demonstrate how the proposed approach meets BR-04 (unified management platform), and AC-31 (consistent policy management across supported operating systems)

c)	The requirements identified as Mandatory in Schedule A such as AC-30 represent Treasury’s minimum requirements, and an Offer that does not satisfy all Mandatory Requirements may be excluded from further evaluation.

3 - Yes. AC-51 may be met through integration with Treasury’s existing endpoint security capabilities, including Microsoft Defender XDR. The application control solution does not need to independently provide malware or ransomware detection where the required outcome can be achieved through integration and correlation with these existing capabilities. Suppliers should clearly describe how their proposed approach satisfies AC-51.

4 - Controlling which scripting engines or interpreter programs are permitted to execute, including through publisher or file hash controls, may form part of meeting AC-21. Suppliers should also confirm whether the proposed solution prevents the execution of unapproved scripts or code through an otherwise approved scripting engine or interpreter.

5 - Carbon Black – enforcement mode. For device numbers and operating system split please see previous clarification responses.

6 - There are approximately 480 applications across the environment. Applications are deployed and maintained through a mix of SCCM and Microsoft Intune (in transition), supplemented by vendor/self-updating applications (eg PatchMyPC) where appropriate. Some applications may also be installed or updated manually where they are not suitable for centrally managed deployment.

7 - Rapid7 integration is not a requirement of the solution. The reference to Rapid7 in Table 10 may be disregarded, and Suppliers are not required to provide pricing for Rapid7 integration.

8 - Treasury does not prescribe a preferred hosting model. Suppliers may propose a supplier-hosted SaaS solution or a customer-hosted solution or both, and should clearly describe the proposed hosting architecture, dependencies and security controls.

For supplier-hosted SaaS solutions, Suppliers should identify all locations where Treasury data is stored, processed, backed up or replicated, including any offshore locations, as part of the SaaS Security Questionnaire. Any proposed offshore storage, processing or replication will be considered as part of Treasury’s security and risk assessment and must comply with the applicable Queensland Government information security requirements referenced in SEC-08 and clarified in previous clarification responses.

publicQuestions.answer:
1 - Already answered in a previous clarification response

2 - Carbon Black. For device numbers and operating system split please see previous clarification response.

3 - 340 rules, 36 policies

4 - Already answered in a previous clarification response

5 - Treasury does not require existing rules to be migrated directly without review. Suppliers may propose migration, rationalisation and/or development of a new policy baseline where appropriate, provided the resulting policy framework meets the requirements of the ITO and supports Treasury’s Essential Eight objectives.

6 - See previous clarification responses. ServiceNow development/configuration is not in scope.

7 - The required Microsoft Sentinel/SIEM integration scope is the forwarding of relevant application control security and audit events to Treasury’s SIEM. The creation of Microsoft Sentinel analytics rules, dashboards, alerting and associated operational use cases should be considered out of scope.

The Supplier is, however, expected to provide sufficient technical documentation and assistance to support Treasury’s interpretation and use of the forwarded events, including event types/codes, fields, severity and other relevant event information required to support Treasury in developing analytics rules and other SIEM content.

8 - Already answered in a previous clarification response

9 - Treasury has not prescribed a specific number of pilot devices/users or fixed production rollout waves. Suppliers should propose an appropriate pilot and staged production rollout approach as part of their Implementation Proposal.

The proposed pilot approach is expected to provide representative testing across each in-scope operating system and device/server type, and should include both standard and privileged user scenarios where applicable. Suppliers should propose sufficient coverage to validate application control policies, user workflows, audit/enforcement behaviour and operational readiness prior to broader production rollout.

10 - The Supplier is not expected to independently certify or attest Treasury’s achievement of Essential Eight Application Control Maturity Level 2. Treasury will retain responsibility for its Essential Eight maturity assessment.

11 - Critical business systems requiring specialist application-owner validation will be identified and provided to the successful Supplier during implementation planning. These systems have lower environments that can be used to support validation and testing during the pilot phase, prior to enforcement in production.

12 - Treasury has not prescribed specific after-hours implementation requirements, change freeze periods or restricted deployment windows as part of the ITO. These will be agreed with the successful Supplier during implementation planning and will be subject to Treasury’s change management and operational requirements.

Suppliers should identify any assumptions regarding implementation windows in their Implementation Proposal and allow for deployment activities to be scheduled appropriately to minimise disruption to Treasury operations. Treasury operates flexible change management approval processes to support delivery timeframes, including the ability to accommodate out-of-session change approvals outside the standard weekly CAB cycle where required.

Where production implementation activities are disruptive or carry unacceptable risk and require after-hours deployment or agreed maintenance windows, these will be coordinated with Treasury as part of implementation planning and change management.

13 - Yes. Treasury resources will be responsible for application-owner engagement, business application approval decisions and final UAT sign-off. The Supplier is expected to support and facilitate these activities as part of the implementation, including providing the necessary technical information, coordinating validation activities, assisting with issue resolution, and providing evidence required to support informed approval and sign-off decisions.

14 - Already answered in a previous clarification response

publicQuestions.answer:
SLES and Ubuntu are not included in the specified scope under AC-30 due to the limited footprint in the environment. Suppliers may describe support for these distributions as additional capability.

Yes these are Windows 11 Enterprise multi-session and are included in the 3000 endpoints.

Already responded to in previous clarification questions

Windows 11: AC-30 requires ongoing compatibility with Windows 11 Enterprise 26H2 and above while within Microsoft’s supported lifecycle. No fixed grace period is specified. Suppliers should state whether support is available at general availability and, if not, identify the proposed support timeframe, any limitations and the approach to maintaining application control protection.

macOS: AC-30 requires compatibility with Apple macOS versions within Apple’s supported lifecycle. Suppliers should identify the supported major and minor versions, any processor architecture or functionality limitations, and their approach and timeframes for supporting new releases.

Suppliers may propose native macOS and RHEL controls as enforcement components, provided the overall solution delivers a unified management platform consistent with BR-04 and consistent policy management under AC-31.

description:
Sutherland Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to tender for the Prince Edward Park Woronora Pedestrian Bridge Renewal Project.

The project involves the demolition of the existing pedestrian bridge and the construction of a new bridge to provide a safe, compliant, and durable pedestrian and cyclist crossing over the Woronora River. The works also include the construction of new shared pedestrian and bicycle path connections associated with the bridge replacement.

The existing bridge, owned by Sutherland Shire Council, provides an important active transport link between Prince Edward Park and Prices Circuit, connecting the northern and southern banks of the Woronora River. Due to the structure's age and condition, the bridge exhibits several defects and no longer meets current design and compliance requirements, affecting its safety, serviceability, and long-term performance.

The Woronora River is an environmentally sensitive area, and the successful Contractor will be required to undertake the works in accordance with all relevant environmental approvals, statutory requirements, and project-specific environmental management measures.

publicQuestions.question:
Further to the RFI answered on 21-Oct, we have this follow-up RFI related to a common flood design basis for tender.

SSC has confirmed an updated flood modelling is being prepared but not available to tenderers, and that the contractor is to determine design flow velocity. Flood velocity & flood level directly govern pier and foundation design, bridge soffit level and approach ramp lengths, and therefore the tender price.

Performance Spec. Table 4.1 dictates the soffit level to be the maximum of (a) 400mm above existing soffit level, (b) 300mm freeboard above the 1% AEP design flood level, or (c) minimum vertical clearance required by TfNSW Maritime.

The 1995 Floodplain Management Study indicates a 1% AEP level of RL 3.8 to 3.9m at the site. Section 10.3 requires flood assessment to include climate change which may increase this level by 0.5-1.0m. To comply with Table 4.1 & Section 10.3 (and subject to post-award flood modelling) the proposed bridge deck soffit level could be as high as RL 5.2m (possibly higher). The existing bridge deck soffit level is approx. 3.1m. Therefore, the proposed bridge soffit would be in the order of 2.1m higher than existing soffit leading to significant cost.

Without a common basis, the tender prices will not be comparable, and the risk of post-award changes will be priced differently by each tenderer.

We request that SSC further reviews these flood modelling concerns and provide direction to all tenderers on what to adopt for both (1) flow velocity, & (2) bridge deck soffit level.
publicQuestions.answer:
Following clarification with SSC's Stormwater Asset Team, a new flood study and hydraulic model for the Woronora River is currently being undertaken. However, Council has been advised that the updated flood modelling data will not be available until March 2027, which is beyond the timeframe required to support the current tender process.

Accordingly, tenderers should not rely on the climate change allowance referenced in Section 10.3 of the Flood Assessment, as updated modelling information is not yet available.

For tender purposes, the replacement pedestrian bridge shall be designed with a maximum soffit level increase of 700 mm above the existing bridge soffit level. Any further flood assessment, hydraulic analysis, or design verification required to support the detailed design will be the responsibility of the successful contractor as part of the Design and Construct process.
