title: Construction of the Warburton (WA) Dialysis Facility
description:
NHS (Ngaanyatjarra Health Service), in partnership with Purple House, is seeking a Head Contractor to deliver a Design and Construct (D&C) commission for a new 4-chair, nurse-assisted haemodialysis facility at Warburton, in the Ngaanyatjarra Lands, Western Australia. The facility is to be delivered as a modular building, prefabricated off-site and transported to Warburton for installation and completion, with a 40-year design life.

Anticipated works commencement is 22 February 2027, with Practical Completion required by 29 October 2027.

The site is located on the Ngaanyatjarra Lands, a remote community in Western Australia. Tenderers must allow for all mobilisation, module transport, accommodation and logistics associated with a remote site of this nature.

vendorPanelDetails.buyerAddress:
Dairy Rd
Fyshwick, Australian Capital Territory 2609
Australia

vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Friday 13 November 2026 05:00 PM (AUS Eastern Daylight Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
Jenarc, as the lead design consultant, has been working with NHS to progress the design of this facility through to 70%, with architectural and all services documentation (mechanical, structural, fire, electrical and hydraulics) now complete and included in this tender package.

As a D&C commission, the successful Head Contractor will take on responsibility for design development and documentation from 70% through to Issue for Construction (IFC), in addition to fabrication, delivery, installation, and all testing and commissioning of the facility.

The project has proceeded through the The Licensing and Accreditation Regulatory Unit's (LARU) AIP (Approved in Principle) pathway associated with its funding. All dialysis, water treatment and biomedical equipment is client-supplied; the Head Contractor is responsible for all associated services rough-in, connections and builder's work in connection required to receive this equipment.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
The successful outcome of this project is the delivery of a fully commissioned, modular 4-chair dialysis facility at Warburton, enabling community members from Warburton and surrounding Western Desert communities to access ongoing dialysis treatment on country. This supports the project's broader objectives of improved treatment attendance, better health outcomes, and continuity of cultural connection, reducing the need for patients to relocate away from family and community for treatment.

Tenderers should demonstrate a methodology and program that reflects genuine experience in remote Aboriginal communities, comparable healthcare and modular construction delivery, and a strong approach to cultural safety, WHS management, and Aboriginal employment and local subcontractor participation throughout delivery.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi,

We just had a couple of queries on the intent behind some of the clauses contained within the specifications. Most of these are resolved by the precedence contained within the contract, however we just wanted to ensure we are offering a solution that aligns with FCRC preferences,

Switchboard internal temperature

E-005 requires the switchboard internal ambient temperature to remain at or below 35°C during normal operation. This would require air conditioning, particularly as the typical designs specify the board be designed for 40 degrees ambient.

Could Council please confirm whether the 35°C internal temperature limit is mandatory for these installations, or whether compliance may be demonstrated through the switchboard temperature-rise assessment under the nominated ambient conditions?

Outdoor switchboard IP rating

E-005 requires external switchboards to be IP56 or better. E-002 also specifies IP66 for outdoor switchboards exposed directly to the elements, with IP56 applying where the switchboard is installed under a suitable shelter.

Could Council please confirm that IP56 is acceptable at each nominated site, or identify any sites where an IP66 enclosure is required due to direct weather exposure?

SMS alarm dialler

The preferred-equipment schedule identifies an Australis M2M SMS alarm dialler; however, the dialler is not included in the listed Council free-issued equipment.

Could Council please confirm whether the SMS dialler will be free issue by Council or is to be included within the contractor’s scope?

Thank you

publicQuestions.question: For the new clear water tanks, can you confirm if the tank, roof, access and platform are to be part of a D&C package or detail designed? Typically specialist reservoir contractor want to design this themselves to suit their standard forms and roof design..
publicQuestions.answer: The intention is that the tank, roof, access and platform will be part of a D&C package. The design consultant will however need to include these items in a preliminary design and develop a detailed design package which specifies these items in adequate detail to capture Council requirements and result in compliant fit for purpose assets.

publicQuestions.question:
Can you confirm the scope for the design of the sludge lagoons?

- The supporting documents indicates that under-drains, polymer dosing and supernatant pump station and rising main are required but they are not mentioned in the brief

- Do the sludge lagoons require a liner? If so what is expected (poly, concrete, clay etc)

- Will the supernatant continue to discharge to the river or returned to the plant?
publicQuestions.answer:
All supporting infrastructure such as under-drains, polymer dosing connections, pump stations and pipework for the sludge lagoons will form part of the scope for this project. As a guide please refer to Option 2 in supporting document 11. Note that since the completion of supporting document 11, Council has acquired additional land that can accommodate larger sludge lagoons.

Sludge lagoons will require a liner which can be assumed to be clay for responding to this tender.

Supernatant is to be returned to the plant.

publicQuestions.question:
The tender questions response by MRC dated from the 16th of October 2026 stated the following:

"The intention is that the tank, roof, access and platform will be part of a D&C package. The design consultant will however need to include these items in a preliminary design and develop a detailed design package which specifies these items in adequate detail to capture Council requirements and result in compliant fit for purpose assets.'

Based on the Services Brief, Section 3.6, could council please re-clarify if MRC requires a complete and separate construction ready Detailed Design and Engineering Specifications for the filtered water storage tanks and sludge lagoons. The Detailed Design Package would then be tendered by council for Construction only. The last sentence of Section 3.6 states the following;

"The Detailed Design should be completed at an appropriate level to include in contract documentation for a design and construct construction tender.'

Could council please clarify the project requirements for the Detailed Design Package will it be used for Construction only or a Design and Construction tender.
publicQuestions.answer: The Detailed Design package will be used for a Design and Construction tender.

publicQuestions.question:
We have a few queries pertaining to this Request. Please see below:

1.	Can Council please confirm if the new Clear Water Storage Tanks will be connected to the existing transfer pump station?

2.	Can Council please clarify the response yesterday, ‘The Detailed Design package will be used for a Design and Construction tender’? Our reading of the Service Brief seems to indicate the Consultant will design up to IFC with a construction only contract apart from the tanks, roof access and platforms which will be design and construct.

3.	Can Council advise if they have a preferred surveying company?

4.	Will Council provide values for the Provisional Items or are these to be priced by the Consultant?
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The new Clear Water Storage Tanks will be connected to the existing transfer pump station.

2. For further clarification, the Detailed Design package prepared by the consultant is to form part of a design and construction tender. The Detailed Design package is to consider all aspects of design for the Clear Water Storage and Sludge Lagoon projects and specify adequate detail to capture Council requirements and result in compliant fit for purpose assets. For aspects of design where there is value for Council in the Construction contractor having flexibility to provide their own design, these items will only have minimum requirements established in the Detailed Design package. A design and construct tender is proposed to ensure best value is provided for Council. Consultants should outline any assumptions that have been made in pricing the Detailed Design Package in the submission.

3. Council does not have a preferred surveying company.

4. The Consultant is to provide pricing for Provisional items. Assumptions that have been used in pricing provisional items should be clearly outlined in submissions.

publicQuestions.question:
Hi there,

Hoping you can provide some clarification on the following:

•	Where is the trails and infrastructure tender up to, and what are the design, construction and handover timeframes?

•	What sort of input are they expecting from us while the D&C work is underway—design reviews, site meetings, commissioning?

•	Do they have a sense of when you might want to start procuring the long-term operator?

•	Is there an indicative budget or expected level of effort for this contract?

•	How many in person Palm Island visits should be catered for in our milestone prices?

•	For booking and data systems, are you expecting us to recommend requirements, or actually select and set up a system? Who would cover licences and ongoing costs?

•	If the D&C program shifts and delays readiness or operator procurement, how would the contract program and fees be adjusted?

Thank you
publicQuestions.answer:
D&C procurement and program

The separate Walking Trails D&C procurement is currently in market and is scheduled to close on 6 November 2026 at 2:00 PM AEST, with contract award targeted for early December 2026. Construction is currently anticipated to occur approximately April–December 2027, followed by commissioning and operational-readiness activities during January–March 2028. These dates are indicative and subject to the outcome of the D&C procurement and final contractor program.

Input during D&C delivery

The Partner is expected to provide tourism, commercial, visitor-experience and operational-readiness input through relevant design reviews, interface workshops/meetings, commissioning, handover and readiness reviews as required. The Partner's role is advisory and does not transfer design or construction responsibility from the D&C Contractor.

Future Tourism Operating Partner procurement

Council expects this procurement to commence once the D&C design and delivery have progressed sufficiently to provide reasonable certainty regarding the infrastructure, operating requirements and anticipated Commercial Opening. Indicatively, Council expects this to occur during 2027, sufficiently ahead of opening to allow for procurement, appointment and operator mobilisation.

Budget / level of effort

Council has not nominated an indicative budget. Tenderers should propose and price the resources and level of effort they consider necessary to deliver the specified outcomes and milestone deliverables, clearly identifying relevant assumptions.

Palm Island visits

Council has not prescribed a fixed number of in-person visits. Tenderers should include an appropriate allowance within their milestone pricing based on their proposed methodology and clearly state their assumptions. Where Council subsequently requests materially additional attendance beyond the accepted scope and methodology, this would be managed in accordance with the Contract.

Booking and data systems

The primary requirement is to develop and recommend the functional, commercial, data, ownership, integration and interoperability requirements for the future operating environment. The Partner is not expected under the current scope to procure and operate an ongoing booking platform. Any specific pre-opening implementation activity would require Council direction. Ongoing system licences and operating costs would ultimately be allocated between Council and/or the future Tourism Operating Partner through the approved operating model and future operator procurement.

Changes to the D&C program

The Partner's program is expected to remain aligned with the D&C delivery program. If the D&C program changes, the services program would be updated accordingly. A change in timing alone does not automatically result in an adjustment to fees. Where a change results in material additional or changed Services, any adjustment would require prior Council approval and be managed through the Contract's Variation and/or Schedule of Rates provisions.

publicQuestions.question: Could you please confirm whether commercial playground and outdoor fitness suppliers are expected to apply for this panel? publicQuestions.answer:
•	Commercial playground and outdoor fitness suppliers may submit a tender where they can demonstrate capability within one or more of the nominated panel categories and satisfy the tender requirements.

publicQuestions.question:
Specification 6 (Page 12) and Specification 13 (Page 20) – Part B: MCC-26-334204 Minor & Major Civil Works Panel

Tenderers seek clarification regarding Council's expectations in relation to the contractual departures process. Specifically, does Council require:

1.	A legal review and contractual departures schedule to be submitted only against the Deed of Standing Offer, with the tenderer reserving the right to review and negotiate the contract applicable to each individual engagement under the Deed; or

2.	A legal review and contractual departures schedule to be submitted only against:

o	The Deed of Standing Offer;

o	Option 1 – MCC Purchase Order Terms & Conditions; and/or

o	Option 2 – MCC Minor Works Contract (Construct Only),

o	With the tenderer reserving the right to review and negotiate any alternative contract selected from the nominated options at the time of engagement (if required).; or

3.	A legal review of the Deed of Standing Offer and all seven (7) nominated contract options, with contractual departures submitted for each individual document.

In addition, tenderers note that AS2124 appears to be referenced as both Option 5 and Option 8. Could Council please confirm whether this duplication is intentional, or whether an alternative contract was intended to be listed for one of these options?

If Council's intention is for proponents to undertake a full legal review and prepare contractual departures against the Deed of Standing Offer and all nominated contract options at tender stage, this would represent a significant commitment of legal and commercial resources. Given the extent of the documentation and the uncertainty as to which contract may ultimately apply to any future engagement, tenderers request confirmation of Council's expectations in this regard.

Should a review of all contract options be required, consideration of an extension to the tender closing date may be warranted to allow sufficient time for a thorough assessment and preparation of departures.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your question Abbey.

Council does not require tenderers to undertake a full legal review of, or submit contractual departures against, all nominated contract options at the tender stage. As a minimum, tenderers should identify any proposed departures or qualifications to the Deed of Standing Offer as part of their tender submission.

Tenderers may also identify departures against other nominated contract forms if they wish; however, this is not mandatory at this stage.

Should a tenderer be appointed to the panel, any contract-specific departures relating to the form of contract selected for an individual engagement may be considered at that time.

With respect to the reference to AS2124 appearing as both Option 5 and Option 8, this is intentional. AS2124 may be utilised for projects both above and below the applicable $1 million threshold, depending on the nature and requirements of the engagement.

No extension to the tender closing date is proposed at this time.

publicQuestions.question:
Could Council please confirm whether it is interested in receiving proposals under MCC-26-334204 – Minor & Major Civil Works Panel from specialist providers offering one or more of the following services:

Underground utility locating using electromagnetic methods and ground penetrating radar, utility mapping and targeted service verification through non-destructive digging/potholing.

Concrete scanning, CCTV drainage inspections, pipe tracing and drainage asset mapping.

Detail and level, topographic, engineering, construction set-out, as-built and boundary surveys.

3D laser scanning, point clouds and Building Information Modelling (BIM).

Measured building surveys, including floor plans, elevations and sections.

Part B, section 2, excludes professional consulting services such as surveying unless incorporated into and directly associated with the civil works.

With this restriction in mind, could Council please clarify:

Eligibility and direct engagement: Would a tender limited to these specialist services be eligible as a conforming tender, without the tenderer undertaking broader civil construction? Could Council engage these specialists directly, or would their services need to be provided through an appointed civil works contractor?

Categories and pricing worksheets: If specialist proposals are eligible, which service categories and pricing worksheets should be completed? Can tenderers nominate and price only the services they offer?

Pricing entries and charges: How should tenderers treat pre-populated rates and items they do not offer in the pricing workbook? Where should minimum attendance charges, travel/mobilisation, accommodation and after-hours rates be recorded so these form part of a conforming tender?

Relevant experience: Would completed utility investigation, surveying or scanning projects satisfy the relevant experience assessment for specialist providers, including projects delivered as a specialist subcontractor rather than the principal civil contractor?

Insurance: Part D lists $20 million for comprehensive motor vehicle insurance, while Part B, clause 8(c), refers to the vehicle’s full market value. Does the $20 million requirement relate to motor vehicle third-party property damage cover? Please also confirm whether contract works insurance would be required for specialist locating, scanning or surveying engagements that involve no construction.

Contract terms: Which of the contract forms listed in Part B, section 6, would Council apply to direct specialist engagements? How would construction-specific obligations be treated where they are unrelated to the specialist services being supplied?

Other procurement opportunities: If these specialist services fall outside this panel, is there another Council panel or planned procurement through which specialist providers should seek consideration?
publicQuestions.answer:
Good afternoon,

This panel is intended to establish a panel of principal civil works contractors. Accordingly, Council will not consider submissions from specialist contractors offering only services such as utility locating, surveying, scanning, mapping, CCTV inspections, or similar specialist services.

Specialist services, including service locating and surveying, are covered under separate panels. Suppliers are encouraged to monitor VendorPanel for future opportunities.

publicQuestions.question:

publicQuestions.answer:

title: RFT260109 Rolleston WTP and WWTP Chlorination Systems
description:
Background Information

Central Highlands Regional Council (CHRC) is seeking new gas chlorination systems at Rolleston WTP, Rolleston WWTP, Dame St WTP Springsure and Twin Tanks WTP Springsure. The works are divided into four (4) Separable Portions, with the requirements and price for each site identified separately.

The chlorination packages will differ in size, capacity, operating requirements and site arrangements. Each Separable Portion will have its own design and performance specification. Tenderers must assess each site individually.

3.1 Purpose of the early tender release

Council is releasing this RFT while the site designs are progressing. The 50% design for Rolleston WTP is included with the initial release. This early release gives suppliers time to understand the project, prepare their tender approach, begin consultation with manufacturers and specialist subcontractors, and get ready for the remaining Separable Portions.

Tenderers should use this period to explore suitable equipment options, confirm manufacturing capacity and delivery lead times, and identify matters requiring clarification from Council.

3.2 Progressive issue of design packages

The remaining site designs and performance specifications will be released by formal addenda over the next three to four weeks following the initial RFT release. Further information or revisions for Rolleston WTP may also be issued during this period. A table shows indicative availability targets. Council will confirm releases and any revised dates through addenda.

3.3 Staged delivery at Rolleston WTP

The Rolleston WTP chlorination works form part of a wider treatment plant upgrade that will be delivered in stages. The package includes pre-chlorination and post-chlorination within Separable Portion One (1). Installation of the new chlorination facility must be coordinated with the clear water tank works, associated pipework and other upgrade activities.

Some installation work may be completed before the new tank and pipework arrangements are ready for connection. Final connections, commissioning and transfer to the new chlorination system must therefore be planned around the readiness of the wider plant upgrade. The existing disinfection system must remain available until Council authorizes the changeover and the new arrangements are ready to operate safely.

Tenderers must allow for coordination with Council operations and other contractors, staged access, and a planned changeover that maintains treatment. The detailed staging requirements and interfaces will be provided with the Rolleston WTP design information and subsequent addenda.

Particulars of Goods and Services

4.1 Separable Portions

SP1 - Rolleston WTP - Gas chlorination at Rolleston WTP in a single facility providing both pre and post chlorination.

SP2 - Rolleston WWTP - Gas chlorination at Rolleston Wastewater Treatment Plant.

SP3 - Dame St WTP - Gas chlorination at Dame St WTP.

SP4 - Twin Tanks WTP - Gas chlorination at Twin Tanks WTP.

4.2 What Council requires from the market

Each Separable Portion is a complete design and construct package. The Contractor must take the relevant Council design information and performance specification through to a completed, operating chlorination system at that site. This includes coordinating all design, manufacturing, supply, installation and commissioning activities, including work undertaken by manufacturers and specialist subcontractors.

Design: Review the issued site information and performance specifications and develop the detailed design for the package in consultation with Council. Coordinate the building, civil, structural, mechanical, electrical, instrumentation and control disciplines required by that site package, including connections and interfaces with the existing plant.

Manufacture and supply: Arrange the manufacture or procurement of the equipment and components required for each site. Coordinate manufacturer input, confirm equipment suitability and lead times, and manage supply and delivery so that the complete package meets the agreed design and program.

Installation: Install and connect the chlorination system and complete the associated works allocated to the Contractor in the site package. Coordinate site activities with Council operations and other contractors, including access, shutdowns and changeovers needed to maintain treatment operations.

Commissioning and handover: Test and commission each site’s completed system, demonstrate that it meets the relevant performance requirements, and provide operator training, operating manuals and as-built information.

Council requires practical, reliable systems suited to each plant’s operating needs and able to be operated and maintained by Council personnel.

The individual site packages will define equipment duties, capacities, layouts, technical requirements and performance criteria. Supporting site information will be included as available.

Please see Part 2 - Specification for further details.

title: 1576-2026 -EOI Provision, Installation & Operation of Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Infrastructure
description:
Council is seeking Expressions of Interest (EOI) from suitably qualified charge point operators (CPOs) interested in installing, operating and maintaining public electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure at Council-owned sites across the municipality.

Council has identified eight potential sites for the installation of public EV charging infrastructure. Respondents may nominate one or more of these sites and may also propose alternative sites within Banyule for Council’s consideration.

Council’s preferred approach is to facilitate the commercial rollout of public EV charging infrastructure through an agreement with successful respondents. Under the proposed arrangement, successful respondents will be responsible for funding, installing, operating and maintaining the charging infrastructure for the agreed term, and will pay Council an annual fee for each approved site, in accordance with the final agreement.

Respondents are invited to outline their proposed sites, charging solutions, commercial offer, delivery approach and ongoing operating arrangements. Council is seeking proposals that demonstrate technical capability, commercial viability, reliable service delivery and accessible public charging for the community.

This EOI is intended to help Council understand the market’s interest, capabilities and proposed solutions before determining the next steps in the procurement process.

The Yarra River runs along the City’s south border while the west is defined by Darebin Creek.

Banyule’s landscape is gently to steeply undulating, apart from some relatively flat land in the west and on the river floodplains. Native vegetation flourishes in the east and north-east, while exotic trees and shrubs dominate the City’s southern and western parts.

title: Cultural Heritage Management, Arts, Interpretation and Visitor Experience Design Services
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council invites tenders from suitably qualified and experienced consultants to provide Cultural Heritage Management, Arts, Interpretation and Visitor Experience Design Services across three Council capital projects:

Indigenous and Arts Installation Precinct (Beachfront Cultural Walk) – Cultural heritage management, cultural engagement, arts curation, artwork and sculpture design, storytelling, interpretive signage, wayfinding and inclusive visitor experience design.

Walking Trails and Tourism Activation Project (including Cultural Welcome Precinct) – Cultural heritage management, negotiation of cultural heritage agreements, construction-phase compliance oversight, arts curation, cultural interpretation, artwork, signage, wayfinding and visitor experience design.

Rodeo Grounds New Subdivision – Cultural heritage management, stakeholder engagement, negotiation of cultural heritage agreements and compliance oversight during design and construction.

The successful consultant will act on Council's behalf, working closely with elected Council, Traditional Owners, Elders, community representatives, artists, project consultants and construction contractors.

The engagement includes the development of complete, culturally approved, construction-ready specialist design documentation for relevant artwork, cultural installations, interpretation, signage, wayfinding and visitor experience elements, enabling implementation through Council's separate construction contracts.

Council seeks a single lead consultant capable of coordinating the full scope, supported by specialist subcontractors or a multidisciplinary team where appropriate.

Location: Palm Island, Queensland. Services may be undertaken remotely where appropriate, with on-island attendance required for stakeholder engagement, cultural consultations, site inspections and project coordination.

Anticipated commencement: December 2026, with an initial 12-month engagement and provision for extension in accordance with the tender documents.

Further requirements are detailed in the Invitation to Tender documentation.

vendorPanelDetails.background:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council is progressing several significant capital projects involving cultural infrastructure, tourism development, public spaces and residential land development.

The Indigenous and Arts Installation Precinct (Cultural Walk) has undergone design development and community engagement, with construction to be delivered under a separate contract. The Walking Trails and Tourism Activation Project, including the Cultural Welcome Precinct, is being progressed through a Design and Construct procurement. The Rodeo Grounds New Subdivision is also progressing through planning, design and development activities.

Council has commissioned cultural engagement, planning and design work for the Cultural Walk and Walking Trails projects, including the GHD Cultural Installation Engagement Outcomes Report (December 2023) and the Walking Trails Engagement Outcomes Report (June 2026). The successful consultant will be expected to review and build upon this existing work, avoiding unnecessary duplication.

Key requirements and project interfaces include:

Working collaboratively with Council, Traditional Owners, Elders, cultural knowledge holders, community representatives, artists and relevant stakeholders.

Coordinating with Council-appointed project managers, architects, engineers, landscape architects, designers, construction contractors and tourism consultants.

Ensuring compliance with applicable Aboriginal cultural heritage legislation, native title arrangements, cultural protocols and project-specific agreements.

Respecting cultural authority, confidentiality, Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property rights, and appropriate cultural approval processes.

Developing coordinated, construction-ready specialist designs that integrate with existing and proposed infrastructure and can be implemented through Council's separate construction contracts.

Ensuring consistency in cultural interpretation, storytelling, wayfinding and visitor experience across the Cultural Walk, Cultural Welcome Precinct and Walking Trails.

Considering accessibility, durability, maintainability and suitability for Palm Island's tropical coastal environment.

Coordinating specialist engineering and technical interfaces where required to complete the design documentation.

Council intends to retain direct control over cultural governance and the approval of cultural content and specialist designs. The consultant will be responsible for developing, coordinating and documenting the relevant design packages and providing implementation support.

Tenderers may propose a multidisciplinary team or specialist subcontractors, provided a single lead contracting entity assumes responsibility for the complete scope.

Relevant background reports, specifications and other reference documentation will be provided through the tender process as applicable. Tenderers should refer to Part B – Specification for the detailed scope, deliverables and responsibilities.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council seeks to achieve culturally appropriate, technically coordinated and high-quality outcomes across the three projects through the engagement of a suitably qualified multidisciplinary consultant.

Desired outcomes include:

- Cultural Heritage Management: Effective engagement with Traditional Owners, Elders and relevant cultural parties; timely negotiation and implementation of cultural heritage agreements; and appropriate compliance oversight throughout design and construction.

- Cultural Governance and Community Participation: Meaningful involvement of the Palm Island community, with appropriate cultural validation, consent, recognition and protection of Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.

- Complete Specialist Design: Delivery of culturally approved, construction-ready designs and technical specifications for artwork, sculptures, cultural installations, storytelling, interpretive signage, wayfinding and visitor information.

- Integrated Visitor Experience: A coherent, accessible and inclusive visitor journey connecting the Cultural Walk, Cultural Welcome Precinct and Walking Trails, with consistent wayfinding and complementary cultural interpretation.

- Local Economic and Cultural Benefits: Opportunities for Palm Island artists, cultural practitioners, Indigenous businesses and community organisations to participate in the design and implementation of cultural elements.

- Effective Project Coordination: Collaborative engagement with Council's project consultants, construction contractors and tourism advisers, ensuring designs are technically compatible with existing infrastructure and construction arrangements.

- Cost Transparency: Progressive cost estimates for proposed cultural and artistic elements, supporting Council's funding decisions and any required construction contract variations.

- Implementation Support: Timely review of contractor submissions, shop drawings, samples and installations to ensure the completed works reflect the approved cultural and specialist designs.

Additional desirable capabilities include:

- Demonstrated experience delivering comparable projects in Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities, particularly regional and remote locations.

- Established relationships with Indigenous artists, cultural practitioners and specialist fabricators.

- Expertise in universal design, accessible information, interpretive exhibitions and digital storytelling.

- Ability to coordinate specialist engineering, fabrication requirements and technical certification.

- Experience integrating cultural interpretation with tourism infrastructure, landscape architecture and public-realm projects.

Service expectations and conditions:

- The consultant must nominate suitably qualified key personnel, maintain appropriate professional indemnity and public liability insurance, and comply with relevant legislation, cultural protocols, confidentiality requirements and Council's contractual conditions.

- Services must be delivered in accordance with agreed programmes, design approval processes, reporting requirements and performance measures. The consultant must promptly identify and escalate matters affecting cultural approvals, project delivery, design coordination, programme or cost.

- All specialist designs and deliverables must be appropriately documented, reviewed and approved before implementation. The consultant must provide editable design files, technical specifications, cultural approval records and relevant handover documentation, subject to applicable intellectual property and cultural permissions.

The overarching objective is to ensure that Council's capital investments deliver lasting cultural, community and visitor benefits, with culturally authentic outcomes that can be implemented efficiently through the respective construction contracts.

publicQuestions.question:
1. Can Council confirm that all existing town planning approvals and associated planning consultancy responsibilities for the three projects remain with Council's existing appointed parties, and that no separate Town Planner is required under this consultancy?

2. Can Council confirm that existing civil engineering, geotechnical investigations, surveying, overall structural design and building certification remain with the respective project designers or contractors, except for specialist engineering directly related to the artwork, sculpture and interpretation packages?

3. Can Council provide the current Design Responsibility and Interface Matrices, relevant approved drawings, outstanding design items and details of the appointed technical consultants for the three projects?

4. For specialist cultural installations requiring new foundations, lighting, electrical infrastructure or drainage, can Council clarify whether these are to be fully designed by the specialist consultant or completed by existing contractor-side designers following specialist interface requirements?

5. Are there existing cultural heritage consultants, engagement representatives or approved cultural governance arrangements that Council expects the successful consultant to work with?

Thank you.
publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your questions. Council provides the following clarifications.

1. Town Planning Responsibilities

Town planning, development applications, statutory planning approvals and associated planning consultancy services remain Council's responsibility through its existing project arrangements.

The successful Consultant is not required to engage a Town Planner or obtain development approvals. However, its specialist designs must comply with applicable planning requirements and conditions communicated by Council.

2. Engineering, Surveying and Building Certification

The successful Consultant is not responsible for general infrastructure engineering or technical investigations, including civil engineering, geotechnical investigations, surveying, overall structural design or building certification.

These services remain with Council's respective project designers and construction contractors.

The Consultant is responsible for all specialist engineering and certification necessary to deliver its artwork, sculpture, cultural installation, interpretation and wayfinding design packages.

3. Design Responsibilities and Interfaces

Council confirms the following allocation of responsibilities:

Council and existing project consultants:

Overall project coordination and statutory approvals.

General infrastructure design, technical investigations and project-wide engineering.

Management of existing design and construction contracts.

Approval of design responsibility allocations and resolution of contractual overlaps or gaps.

Successful Consultant:

Cultural heritage management across all three projects.

Complete specialist design of artwork, sculptures, cultural installations, interpretation, signage, wayfinding and visitor experience elements for the Cultural Walk and Walking Trails projects.

Specialist engineering, technical specifications, connection and fixing requirements, and certification associated with those designs.

Preparation of construction-ready specialist design packages.

Coordination of technical interfaces with the respective project designers and contractors.

Construction contractors:

Construction-related design and engineering allocated under their contracts.

Shop drawings, fabrication, procurement, installation, testing and commissioning.

Construction quality assurance, compliance and certification associated with their works.

Council retains responsibility for establishing and approving contractual design allocations. The successful Consultant must document the detailed interfaces associated with its specialist scope through Design Responsibility and Interface Matrices.

Council will manage any required amendments to existing construction contract responsibilities.

Relevant drawings, specifications and technical information have been provided in the tender documentation where available. Additional project information and details of appointed consultants will be provided during mobilisation.

4. Foundations, Lighting, Electrical Infrastructure and Drainage

For specialist cultural installations, responsibilities are allocated as follows:

Successful Consultant:

Complete design of the installation, artwork or cultural feature.

Dimensions, materials, structural performance, design loads and fixing/connection requirements.

Specialist engineering and certification associated with the installation.

Lighting and electrical performance requirements, including intended effects, equipment requirements and connection points.

Technical information required by other designers to complete associated infrastructure.

Existing project designers and construction contractors:

Site-specific foundation design, including ground conditions, excavation, reinforcement and supporting structures.

Electrical supply, cabling, distribution and associated infrastructure design.

General drainage and civil infrastructure design.

Construction, installation, testing and commissioning.

Council will resolve any interface requiring an adjustment to existing contractual responsibilities.

The Consultant must provide sufficient technical information for the respective project designers and contractors to complete their works without undertaking further substantive design of the specialist cultural elements.

5. Existing Cultural Heritage Consultants and Governance Arrangements

Council has provided relevant reference documentation, including:

Palm Island Indigenous Land Use Agreement (ILUA).

Palm Island Planning Scheme.

Proposed Tourism Governance, Commercial and Operating Model.

Previous cultural engagement reports, including the GHD Cultural Installation Engagement Outcomes Report and Walking Trails Engagement Outcomes Report.

Relevant project drawings and specifications.

The proposed governance model identifies potential arrangements involving Traditional Owners, Elders, cultural knowledge holders, Rangers and community representatives. It does not constitute a formally approved cultural heritage governance arrangement.

Council's responsibilities:

Coordinate introductions to relevant existing advisers and stakeholders.

Approve project-specific engagement and governance arrangements.

Retain formal contractual, statutory and legal decision-making authority, without replacing the authority of the relevant cultural parties.

Successful Consultant's responsibilities:

Review existing cultural heritage documentation and engagement outcomes.

Identify outstanding cultural heritage requirements for each project.

Develop and implement project-specific cultural engagement and management strategies.

Coordinate consultation and cultural validation processes.

Lead negotiations for cultural heritage agreements for Walking Trails and Rodeo Grounds, in coordination with Council and its legal advisers.

Monitor cultural heritage obligations during design and construction.

Existing reports and proposed governance arrangements are background information and do not replace the need for appropriate cultural consultation, consent or statutory compliance.

publicQuestions.question:
As we prepare a tender for WRKS0045. We have five questions on the tender documents.

- Drawing F200 (Synthetic Cricket Wicket and Concrete Slab Profiles) vs BOQ (C4) and Drawing F150 (Earthworks Volumes)

The profiles show a 200mm VicRoads Type A capping layer above subgrade, under the slab. F150 measures select fill only up to subgrade (588.5 m³), which matches BOQ C4 (590 m³). Is the capping layer, about 130 m³, included in C4, or should we price it as an additional item?

- GB5006B (Layout Plan) vs Part 2 Conditions of Contract (cl 15.6)

The swale runs through the 5m easement at 101 Golf Links Rd and includes removing and reinstating the owner’s fence. Has the City arranged access with the landowner, or does the contractor need to obtain consent? If the contractor does, what notice period should we allow?

- BOQ (C1) vs Drawing F050 (Legend, Note 5)

BOQ C1 says to stockpile stripped topsoil for re-use, and G1 uses reclaimed topsoil. F050 says turf and organic material is disposed of off-site. Please confirm the topsoil is stockpiled for re-use in G1, with only the excess removed.

- BOQ (D5) vs Drawing F320 (Concrete Endwall Detail)

The BOQ lists a precast wingwall to suit the 225mm PVC pipe. F320 shows a precast headwall suitable for a Ø450 outlet. Please confirm the headwall size.

- Specification (5.5 Rubber Matting) and Drawing F700 (Note 1) vs Drawing F200 and GB5006C

The specification and F700 show rubber matting 1000mm high. F200 and GB5006C show 1200mm high. Please confirm the height.

We’d appreciate your responses as early as possible so we can finalise our price.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. The volume in C4 in the BOQ and drawing F150 are assumed to achieve the desired subgrade levels across the entire site and is the total compacted volume of select fill required. The ‘Concrete Slab Profile’ on drawing F200 is indicative only and is not additional.

2. The resident is aware of the works, though the successful contractor will be required to provide notice of the works once a firm start date has been established – typically 2 weeks.

3. Only excess topsoil (prioritising that containing grass / weed material) will need to be removed.

4. Precast headwall is to suit the 225mm PVC drainage pipe.

5. Rubber matting is to be 1000mm high per the specification and drawing F700

title: Butler Bay Sewage Rising Main Replacement – Design and Construct
description:
Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council invites suitably qualified and experienced contractors to submit tenders for the Design and Construction of the Butler Bay Sewage Rising Main Replacement Project (PIASC.2627.BBSRM01) on Palm Island, Queensland.

The project involves the replacement of approximately 3 kilometres of existing sewage rising main between Sewage Pump Station 5 (SPS 5) at Butler Bay and Sewage Pump Station 6 (SPS 6), generally following the existing Butler Bay Road corridor.

The scope includes engineering investigations, hydraulic and detailed design, pipeline supply and installation, associated SPS 5 refurbishment and SPS 6 connection works, temporary sewage bypass arrangements, testing, commissioning, decommissioning and handover.

Council is seeking a fully inclusive, lump-sum Design and Construct solution, with the contractor responsible for design development, construction methodology, materials, freight, mobilisation, workforce accommodation and all associated delivery requirements.

Design investigations and development are intended to occur principally during the 2026–2027 wet season, with construction predominantly during the 2027 dry season. Practical Completion is required by 31 December 2027.

The works will be undertaken on Palm Island, approximately 65 kilometres northwest of Townsville, Queensland. Design and engineering activities may be undertaken remotely, while site investigations and construction will require attendance on Palm Island.

Tender closing: Friday, 27 November 2026 at 2:00 pm Australian Eastern Standard Time (AEST).

Tender documentation, clarification requests and submissions will be managed electronically through VendorPanel.

1 Main St
Palm Island, Queensland 4816
Australia
vendorPanelDetails.buyerDescription: Palm Island Aboriginal Shire Council
vendorPanelDetails.queryCutoffAtRaw: Monday 30 November 2026 02:00 PM (E. Australia Standard Time)
vendorPanelDetails.background:
The existing Butler Bay Sewage Rising Main is approximately 3 kilometres long and has experienced deterioration, corrosion and repeated failures. Hydraulic oversizing has also contributed to low flow velocities, septicity and ongoing operational challenges.

Council intends to replace the existing infrastructure with a reliable, appropriately sized and maintainable sewage rising main that accommodates current demand and forecast growth.

The replacement pipeline must generally follow the existing Butler Bay Road corridor and connect SPS 5 to SPS 6. The proposed solution must be compatible with Council's existing sewerage network, pumping infrastructure, operational requirements and downstream wastewater treatment arrangements.

The tender package includes technical planning information prepared by GANDEN and Peak Services. These documents are provided for reference only and do not constitute a completed detailed design. The successful contractor will be responsible for verifying planning assumptions, undertaking necessary investigations and developing a compliant engineering solution.

Particular consideration must be given to hydraulic performance, pump station interfaces, continuous sewerage service during construction, existing utilities, ground conditions, environmental protection, safe construction methodology and Palm Island's remote logistics.

Council requires a complete, operational and fit-for-purpose Design and Construct solution, delivered in accordance with the technical specification and contract requirements.
vendorPanelDetails.desiredOutcomes:
Council seeks a complete, reliable, safe and cost-effective Design and Construct solution that provides long-term improvements to the performance, resilience and maintainability of the Butler Bay sewerage infrastructure.

Desired project outcomes include:

- Replacement of the deteriorated rising main with an appropriately sized, durable and hydraulically efficient system, compatible with existing and forecast sewerage demand.

- Refurbishment and integration of SPS 5 and associated connection works at SPS 6.

- Continuous and safe sewerage service throughout construction, with effective temporary bypass arrangements.

- Optimised design and construction methodologies that minimise whole-of-life costs, operational risks, environmental impacts and disruption to the community.

- Effective management of Palm Island's remote construction logistics, including freight, equipment, workforce mobilisation and accommodation.

- Completion of design activities principally during the 2026–2027 wet season and construction predominantly during the 2027 dry season.

- Practical Completion by 31 December 2027, including testing, commissioning, as-constructed documentation, operating and maintenance manuals, and operator training.

- Meaningful local employment, training, subcontracting and procurement opportunities for Palm Island residents and businesses.

Contract conditions and warranties:

The project will be delivered under a lump-sum Design and Construct contract based on AS 4902–2000, incorporating Council's special conditions.

The contractor will be responsible for achieving the specified performance requirements, complying with applicable legislation and engineering standards, maintaining appropriate insurances, implementing WHS, quality and environmental management systems, and rectifying defects during the 12-month defects liability period.

Council expects proactive project management, regular progress reporting, updated delivery programs and monthly cashflow forecasts.

Tenderers are encouraged to demonstrate practical innovations and additional benefits that improve value for money, construction efficiency, asset reliability, maintainability and local participation, provided these remain within the specified Butler Bay Road corridor and comply with the tender requirements.

The successful contractor must deliver a fully operational system suitable for Council's ongoing ownership, operation and maintenance.

o	Assess and recommend appropriate precinct management mechanisms such as Special Entertainment Precincts and Community Improvement Districts.

A Tourism Strategy 2027–2037 (TS)

The TS should provide a practical roadmap with clear actionable steps and projects that:

o	Addresses both demand-side and supply-side constraints and opportunities.

o	Delivers a place-based visitor economy strategy focused on shifting the region from low-yield day-tripping and highway ‘pit stops’ to higher-yield overnight visitation.

o	Formulates a clear experience hierarchy that defines current and potential hero experiences and supporting themes.

o	Identifies catalyst projects that would provide a step change in the trajectory of visitor economy development.

o	Guides the continued evolution and maturation of QPRC’s tourism program with respect to marketing, product/experience development, industry capacity building and tourism infrastructure development.

o	Assesses the effectiveness and suitability of continued use of the ‘Treasure Trail’ as an ongoing campaign brand (and de facto destination brand). Development of a new destination brand is not a part of this project, however the strategy should discuss and recommend future destination branding actions.

o	Provide clarity on the brand hierarchy of the region ‘Queanbeyan-Palerang’, the towns (e.g. Queanbeyan, Bungendore and Braidwood) and specific visitor experiences.

o	Considers the need for sustainable destination position that balances economic growth with ecology, community wellbeing and liveability, and cultural preservation.

o	Addresses the strategic linkages with Visit Canberra and adjoining LGAs to capture visitor flows and dispersal, and leverage cross-border synergies.

o	Considers the broader economic context and business environment, and addresses systemic challenges such as workforce attraction and retention in the tourism and hospitality sectors.

o	Is aligned with the NSW Visitor Economy Strategy and the Destination Southern NSW Destination Management Plan to maximise eligibility for future state and federal funding programs.

Both documents should avoid generic, high-level statements and must provide concrete, costed (where appropriate) and prioritised action plans, with lead responsibilities, partner dependencies, potential funding streams and clear KPIs.

publicQuestions.answer:
Thank you for your questions. Please see responses to each question below.

1. Will Council accept relevant Economic Development Strategy and Tourism Strategy projects delivered by nominated key personnel while employed by other organizations, provided their contributions can be substantiated through project evidence and client referees?

Response: Yes

2. Will experience demonstrated by consortium partners or specialist subcontractors be assessed under the 35% Demonstrated Experience and Capability criterion? Does Council distinguish between the experience of the lead bidder and that of its proposed delivery partners?

Response: Yes, experience of all parties will be considered and weighted with respect to the size of their contribution to the project delivery.

3. Must nominated key personnel already be employees of the respondent at the submission deadline, or will Council accept independent consultants, contractors and specialists engaged specifically for the project, provided their availability and commitment are confirmed?

Response: If availability and commitment are confirmed, the key personnel do not need to be currently employed/contracted by the respondent.

4. Are there any minimum years of relevant experience, required professional qualifications or mandatory previous council projects for the nominated project lead and specialist consultants beyond the published evaluation criteria?

Response: No.

5. Can an international consultancy participate as the lead bidder in partnership with an Australian-registered entity? Must every consortium member hold an ABN and GST registration, or is compliance by the contracting lead entity sufficient?

Response: There are no requirements that specifically preclude international consortia, however this should be addressed and explained within the submission.

6. Will Council consider proposals for only the Economic Development Strategy or only the Tourism Strategy? If so, should these be submitted as separate priced components, and will they be evaluated independently?

Response: Respondents may consider submitting for either of, or both, strategies. As some aspects of the projects overlap, efficiencies may be available by one respondent quoting for both, however this is not essential. If a respondent supplies a quotation that itemises the two projects separately, they should indicate if they are willing to be considered for only one of the projects, or if the full quotation is to be considered only in its entirety.

7. How many comparable project references should respondents provide? Will Council accept references relating to work personally delivered by proposed specialists, rather than contracts held by the respondent organisation itself?

Response: There are no minimum requirements; a respondent should provide references that can demonstrate its capability and experience. Yes, references that are applicable to proposed specialists can be accepted.

8. Can Council provide the approved or indicative budget range for the overall project, or separate budget allocations for the Economic Development Strategy and Tourism Strategy?

Response: The publicly-available QPRC Operational Plan 2026-27 allocates $80,000 for a Tourism Strategy. Following scoping of the project and informal market testing, it is anticipated that significant efficiencies can be realised by delivering both projects simultaneously. Respondents may consider submitting a quotation that modestly exceeds the available budget endorsed in the Operational Plan.

Response: The precise consultation schedule will be determined in consultation with the successful respondent and informed by the experience of Council staff and the engaged consultants. 11. Will Council provide the existing strategies, economic studies, asset inventories, visitor information and relevant internal data needed to undertake the assignment?

12. Correct strategy period (RFQ ##2 and 4): Section 2 specifies 2027–2037 for both strategies, while Section 4 specifies 2027–2035. Which planning period should respondents use?

title: 2026/192 Back Creek Bridge - Design and Construction
description:
The City of Boroondara (Council) requires a suitably qualified and experienced Contractor to carry out the following works in accordance with this Request for Tender (RFT) and its attachments. Council invites the tenderer to submit a tender for the provision of the works in a Design and Construct capacity for the Back Creek Bridge project.

The Back Creek Bridge (the Project) involves the design and construction of a new pedestrian and cyclist bridge over Back Creek. The Project also includes the potential construction of an accessible shared path to provide a continuous connection between Denman Avenue and Somerset Road in Glen Iris. The shared path will require a retaining wall along its alignment. The Project supports Council’s vision to improve community connectivity, encourage sustainable transport, and enhance safety and accessibility along the trail.

The Back Creek Reserve in Glen Iris forms part of the broader Back Creek Trail corridor that extends north-south through the City of Boroondara. The corridor is a key element of Council’s open space and active transport network, providing important links between residential areas, local streets, and key community destinations.

At a high level, the proposed works include:

•	A shared pedestrian and cyclist bridge connecting the East and West of the Back Creek Reserve;

•	Handrail, lighting and bollards to the bridge;

•	Shared path connection (Optional item);

•	Retaining Wall (Optional Items) and

•	Design of the Works

 Key objectives of the Back Creek Bridge project are to:

•	Deliver a safe, universally accessible bridge crossing for pedestrians and cyclists.

•	Minimise environmental and hydraulic impacts on Back Creek and surrounding vegetation.

•	Provide a robust, low-maintenance structure with a 100-year design life.

•	Integrate the new paths and retaining wall into existing footpaths and roads with minimal disruption.

A Preliminary Design has been developed by GHD and Stantec for the Works. With neither GHD nor Stantec being engaged to complete any further design requirements under the contract. Council is seeking to engage a Contactor to carry out the design and construction of Works.

The Preliminary Design for the bridge construction has been based on a steel system. Tenderers’ submissions are to be based on a steel system in order to be considered conforming.

However, Council is open to Tenderers proposals for alternative bridge construction systems. Tenderers may submit alternative design options for the bridge construction, together with the reasoning for the proposed alternative(s), such as cost savings, time savings, durability, and/or design life.

Any proposal for an alternative bridge construction system will be deemed non-conforming; however, it may still be considered and accepted by Council.

The Contractor will be required to perform the work strictly in accordance with:

•	the requirements of the Contract; and

•	applicable Australian Standards, building codes, industry standards, the requirements of any authority having jurisdiction over the work, occupational health and safety acts and regulations, and manufacturers' recommendations and requirements.

Tenderers must ensure that they read these Contract Documents fully to ascertain the nature of the work to be performed and the terms on which it is to be performed, as the Contract will be evidenced solely by the Contract Documents.

Tenderers Note - Contract No. 2026/192, Back Creek Bridge - Design and Construct is being released under the conditions of Modified AS4902 Design and Construct Contract - which shall be issued under Addendum No 1 during the week commencing 19/10/26

publicQuestions.question:
Hi Guys,

I have two queries relating to the lighting design for the bridge, that ideally need to be clarified during tender stage.

If you could address these queries for our lighting designer, I would really appreciate it:

1. Amber and 3000 K cannot both be delivered. Amber for wildlife is typically a narrow band source around 590 nm, or phosphor converted amber at roughly 1900 K. A 3000 K luminaire is warm white and retains exactly the short wavelength content that amber exists to remove. Could you confirm which the Principal wants? If it is amber, AS/NZS 1158.3.1 applies a lumen derating below 2500 K, so more installed load is needed for the same compliance figures and colour rendering drops substantially.

2. No lighting subcategory has been nominated, and this one decides whether handrail luminaires can comply at all. At PP3 a point vertical illuminance of 0.1 lx applies at 1.5 m above the path. At PP4 and PP5 the standard provides that vertical illuminance need not be applied to luminaires mounted at 1.5 m or less — and handrail lights sit below that height. Please provide the subcategory and its basis?

Thanks and regards.
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Colour temperature / amber lighting

Council is not seeking a true amber lighting solution. Rather, Council's preference is for a low colour temperature luminaire that minimises blue light content while maintaining appropriate lighting performance and colour rendering. The advice provided by Council's biodiversity team is that lighting should be at or below 3000K, with a preference for 2700K where feasible in this environmentally sensitive location.

Accordingly, please proceed on the basis of a warm-white LED solution (preferably 2700K, otherwise not exceeding 3000K), rather than a monochromatic or phosphor-converted amber luminaire. This approach aligns with Council's draft lighting guidance for biodiversity corridors, which seeks to reduce potential impacts on fauna through lower colour temperature lighting, while still achieving the required lighting outcomes.

2. Lighting subcategory

The intention is for the shared user path to be designed to AS/NZS 1158 Category PP3, reflecting the anticipated usage levels of the path.

The lighting design should therefore demonstrate compliance with the requirements of PP3. If your assessment identifies that the proposed handrail-mounted luminaires alone cannot achieve compliance with the applicable PP3 criteria, including vertical illuminance requirements where relevant, please advise and provide recommendations for alternative arrangements that would achieve compliance whilst minimising ecological impacts, light spill and impacts on nearby residents. Council's preference remains to keep lighting as low-key as practical within the biodiversity corridor and in close proximity to private properties. Council would not support pole-mounted lighting on the bridge structure. Where vertical illuminance requirements cannot reasonably be achieved through handrail-mounted lighting alone, this may be documented as a design limitation for Council's consideration and acceptance, provided the design demonstrates that ecological, residential amenity and safety objectives have been appropriately balanced.

publicQuestions.question:
**TRC000595 – Request for clarification**

Dear Procurement Team,

We are preparing a response to the register of pre-qualified suppliers for onsite crushing, screening and production of gravel. Could Council please clarify the following matters?

**1. Annual rate reviews**

Section 6 of the specifications allows suppliers to review and update their indicative rates at twelve-month intervals, while the special conditions exclude the general CPI adjustment clause. Please confirm the process, notice period and approval requirements for annual rate updates, and whether the updated approved rates become the ceilings for subsequent project quotations.

**2. Pricing inclusions and additional charges**

Please confirm whether the per-tonne rates must include ripping and excavation, feed loading, blending, moisture conditioning, finished stockpiling, supervision and site facilities.

Can mobilisation, demobilisation, transport between pits, standby and minimum campaign charges be quoted separately? Please also confirm whether each tonnage band applies to the entire campaign or only the tonnes within that band, including the treatment of quantities at the band boundaries.

**3. Material quality, testing and production delays**

Where Council-supplied source material or a Council-directed blend cannot achieve the required specification, how will trial processing, reblending, reprocessing and associated costs be managed?

Please confirm the payment arrangements for production delays caused by laboratory testing, unavailable water, restricted site access or Council-directed stoppages. How will payable production tonnes be determined where calibrated loader records differ from Council’s stockpile survey?

**4. Project availability, site access and environmental approvals**

What notice will suppliers normally receive before a required commencement date? Can a panel supplier decline an individual RFQ where its plant or personnel are unavailable, without affecting its panel status?

Will each RFQ identify the applicable environmental approvals, permitted activities and operating hours? Please confirm whether Council’s approvals authorise the proposed crushing activities at each site, including roadside borrow pits, and identify any separate approvals Council expects the contractor to hold.

**5. Supervisor qualifications, inductions and plant inspections**

Will Council accept recognised equivalent or superseded versions of RIIRIS301E, RIIWHS301E and RIICOM301E? Please advise how these qualifications should be submitted for acceptance.

Please confirm the arrangements and available dates for quarry inductions and Council VOCC assessments. Could Council also provide complete current minimum safety hardware checklists for the applicable plant, including excavators and any continuation pages not included in the specifications?

**6. Insurance and WHS submission requirements**

The special conditions specify workers compensation, public liability and product liability insurance, while the WHS questionnaire also requests professional indemnity insurance. Please confirm whether professional indemnity insurance is required for this arrangement.

The specifications require a completed WHS systems questionnaire, while the offer response refers to an alternative for contractors already compliant in Council’s contractor management system. Please confirm whether all offerors must submit the questionnaire and supporting evidence regardless of their existing registration status.

Thank you for your assistance.

Kind regards,

Murray Payne

Principal Consultant

Muzza Resource Services

On behalf of Renn Contracting
publicQuestions.answer:
1. Council will make contact with successful offerors approximately one month prior to the contract anniversary date, to provide the opportunity for updated indicative rates which will then be reviewed and approved. Any approved updated indicative rates will then become the ceilings for subsequent project quotations.

2. Confirmed, must include all of the above. If a site requires blasting, it will be done in advance and all offerors will be notified in the request for quote document.

No. There are no mobilisation rates, no standby payments, no campaign rates. Each site crushing activity will be quoted individually during the life of the contract.

3. All costs will be carried by the crushing contractor. Council has extensive quality and testing results for each location. Ad-mixture percentages will be included in the request for quotes. Negotiation of production methodology or alternative blends is not permitted. Each quotation will specify minimum equipment requirements, e.g. Jaw/Impactor, Jaw only will not be permitted.

Each contractor has been made aware of “hold points” for quality testing in the tender documents and can price accordingly. Council uses accredited software to survey finished stockpiles. Should a dispute arise, Council will engage an independent certified surveyor to carry out a field measurement, density testing will be carried out by an independent NATA approved laboratory. Should there still be a discrepancy, Council shall withhold payment and an internal contractual non-conformance will be raised against the crushing contractor. At each individual crushing quotation request, each offeror will be given an opportunity to view the site location and discuss the upcoming job. No payment shall be made for operational stoppages. Council reserves the right to stop crushing activities at any time.

4. Council endeavours to give as much notice as possible for each crushing activity (approx. 6 weeks), however due to the nature of some works, including emergency repairs, this is not always possible. There is no consequence for not quoting on an individual crushing activity.

All crushing activities currently take place on Council’s ERA locations; the contractor does not require any further environmental licences or to make any notifications to the regulator.

5. Council will accept superseded versions as per RSHQ’s table of acceptable qualifications for an appointed site supervisor.

Induction dates will be announced following the completion of the panel selection process and the makeup of the panel is known.

6. Professional indemnity insurance will not be required for pure crushing activities including the supply of the site supervisor and crushing crew as they work under direction and do not advise.

Offerors who have completed the WHS systems questionnaire and provided the supporting documents required and are compliant in Council's contractor management system (Beakon), are not required to provide this again with their submission. However, if unsure if compliant in Beakon or not, it is recommended to provide the completed questionnaire and documents with your submission.

title: CTWW007 - 26/27 - Maryborough Landfill - Cell 9B - Design and Construct
description:
OVERVIEW

Fraser Coast Regional Council is inviting offers from suitably qualified and experienced Tenderers for CTWW007 - 26/27 - Maryborough Landfill: Cell 9B - Design and Construct.

MANDATORY TENDER BRIEFING

A Tender Briefing is mandatory for this tender. The details are outlined below:

Date: Thursday, 29 October 2026

Time: 10:00am (AEST)

Location: Maryborough Landfill - 269 Ariadne Street, Maryborough QLD 4650 - Main Entrance / Site Office

Booking Required: YES

Point of Contact for Booking: Email - procurement@frasercoast.qld.gov.au

Other Details (incl. Dress Code / PPE): High-visibility shirt or vest; long pants; boots; sunscreen and a wide-brim hat

SUBMISSION OF TENDER DOCUMENTS

Please be advised that tender response forms are to be submitted as three (3) documents only and in the following format:

- Non-Price Response Form: PDF including all supporting documentation as one (1) document. This PDF must not contain any price related criteria.

- Price Response Form: Excel

- Contract Amendments and Particulars: Excel

Failure to comply with this requirement may result in a non-conforming offer.

publicQuestions.question:
Can you please clarify if the Contractor is to provide CQA Engineer during construction in order for the D&C team to certify the construction, Or will the independent CQA to be engaged by the Principal be certifying the Construction.

Can Council please confirm who the Independent CQA consultant will be.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #1.

publicQuestions.question:
Good afternoon,

Could the council please provide the following in CAD format:

1.	The Cell 9A as-constructed survey (Surveyors@Work, Oct 2024) and the Cell 9A IFC drawings, both currently provided as PDF only.

2.	The Surveyors@Work Maryborough Landfill Site survey of June 2026, or any other current survey of the Cell 9B area.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #2

publicQuestions.question:
Good morning,

We respectfully request a two-week extension to the closing date for this tender.

Given the D&C nature of the project, additional time would allow us to undertake a more comprehensive review of the design requirements and develop our proposed design solution, including appropriate consideration of constructability and delivery methodology.

The additional time would also allow our key subcontractors and suppliers to properly review the requirements and provide comprehensive and competitive quotations, ensuring these inputs are fully considered within our design, methodology and pricing.

Thank you for considering this request, we look forward to your response.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #2

publicQuestions.question: Please confirm if the designing consultant is the same as the onsite CQA consultant?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #2

publicQuestions.question: We note the previous Cell 9A drawings detail LLDPE for the geomembrane layer. The current Cell 9B BOQ item 6.3 details HDPE for the geomembrane layer. Please confirm what material is required for the construction of Cell 9B?
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #2

publicQuestions.question:
1.	Please provide the Cell 9A Design Report and/or supporting design basis information, if available.

2.	Please provide available recent and historical groundwater monitoring data for the site.

3.	Please provide details of the Cell 9A leachate extraction/pumping system, including pump specifications, operating levels and available historical pumping records.

4.	Please provide any additional historical geotechnical or hydrogeological investigations for the site, including investigations undertaken for Cell 9A.

5.	Please confirm the basis for the inferred natural ground surface shown on the Cell 9A design drawings and provide supporting information, if available.

6.	Please provide the current site Surface Water Management Plan and any associated drainage drawings relevant to Cell 9B.

7.	Please confirm whether the Cell 9B scope includes the leachate extraction/pumping system beyond the collection pipework and sump riser and, if so, provide the required performance and interface requirements.

8.	Please confirm whether the Cell 9B scope requires a landfill gas extraction system beyond the groundwater/gas relief system identified in the tender documents and, if so, provide the required performance and interface requirements.

9.	Please provide any available information confirming the extent and levels of existing waste and known leachate adjacent to the Cell 9B excavation and tie-in areas.
publicQuestions.answer: Please refer to Addendum #4 and attachments.

title: FOGO Marketing, Engagement, Education and Behaviour Change Project
description:
MidCoast Council invites tenders from suitably qualified consultants to design, develop, deliver and evaluate a comprehensive Food Organics and Garden Organics (FOGO) marketing, engagement, education and behaviour change campaign.

The successful Consultant will translate Council’s Education and Behaviour Change Strategy and Plan Framework into a coordinated campaign that helps residents understand the new service, prepare for its introduction and correctly separate food and garden organics.

Services include community research and audience analysis; behaviour change and campaign planning; creative development and message testing; production of accessible content and reusable engagement materials; media planning and buying; community outreach and face-to-face engagement; launch support; ongoing reinforcement; and evaluation and handover.

Tenderers must propose the quantities, formats, frequency, coverage and resources for each deliverable for Council’s assessment, supported by pricing and estimated professional effort in the response schedules.
